Lineolate means marked with fine lines, which is striated.
Dimpled means with small pits, which is foveate.
'Sparsely' limits the amount of leaves, and 'leafy' loses it. It would assert a well-leaved part.
Narrow is a degree word. The shape is still oblong.
Pliable means bendable, which is PATO flexible.
Chlorophyllose means containing chlorophyll, so green.
Hardly visible means inconspicuous.
Hornless means not horned. I could not read the FLOPO_0991029 row in the value-term file, so I did not check its definition.
Crimped means finely wavy or curled, which fits crisped.
Salient means standing out, which is prominent.
Fistulous means hollow, like a pipe.
Equal in size matches the definition of the FLOPO equal class, which is a size quality of a set of like parts.

The target 'floating' means resting on the water surface. Free-floating also means not attached to the ground, and it can mean submerged. The class's own note says free-floating plants must be kept apart from floating organs.
Cuculliform means hood-shaped, which is cucullate.
Inequal is a variant spelling of unequal.
Venate means having veins. PO vascular bundle has the synonym vein.
Cernuous means nodding or drooping.
Apiculate is a short, sharp, flexible tip. Mucronulate is a small stiff mucro. They are close but not the same, and the extra word 'short' is lost.
Samaroid means like a samara, a winged fruit, so winged.
PO primary root has the synonym tap root.
Narrow-ovate is ovate with a degree word. The target is the temporary ovate class.
Agglutinated means glued together without fusion, which matches coherent.
Barbulate means minutely bearded, which fits bearded. The small size is lost.
Pedately divided means pedate.
Loculicidally dehiscent means loculicidal.
Adhering means sticking to another structure, which matches adherent.
PATO falciform lists hooked as a synonym, so 'not hooked' maps to not falciform.
Rootless means root absent.
The rule negates the anastomosing value, which is the right meaning.
Soft-wooded describes the wood, not the whole bearer. Mapping it to plain 'soft' loses the wood. The bearer should be wood.
Spur-like means spur shaped.
Tape-like means strap-shaped.
Unpleasant alone can describe smell or taste. It is foetid only when the description is about smell.
Dichotomously forked means bifurcated. The word 'dichotomously' is lost but the meaning holds.
PATO falciform lists hooked as a synonym.
The quality 'inconspicuous' belongs to the veins, not to the bearer. The bearer should be vein, or the rule should be limited to veined parts.
Clawlike means claw-shaped.
Subrotund means nearly round, which is subcircular.
Hood-like means cucullate.
Exarillate means without an aril.
Stringy means fibrous in texture.
Tuberiferous means bearing tubers.
Upswept means curving upward, which is ascending.
Without lenticels means lenticel absent.
The subglabrous definition is 'nearly glabrous'.
Elongating in fruit means the part keeps growing after flowering, which is accrescent. The part constraint is sensible.
Not projecting means not protruding.
Partitioned means divided by septa, so septum present.
Strap-like means strap-shaped.
Conglomerate means clustered, and PATO aggregated lists clustered as a synonym.
Subrotundate is a variant of subrotund, which is subcircular.
Keel-like means keel-shaped.
Not keeled is the negation of keel-shaped.
Intricate branching or twigs means tangled or interwoven.
Resin dots are glands in the tissue, so this matches gland-dotted.
Sharply acute is acute in the botanical sense, with the sides converging to a sharp point.
The constraint keeps this to stem, whole plant and root, where clinging means climbing by attachment.
Hook-like means hooked, which is a listed synonym of falciform.
Layered means stratified for tissues and coverings. For shoots or branches it can mean tiers, or layering as propagation.
Utriculate means bearing a utricle, so a utricle fruit is present. Carex-type uses describe an inflated sac and are less certain.
Spindly means thin and elongate. It also suggests weak, which is lost.
Leafy loses 'densely'. Dense leaf arrangement is part of the meaning.
Nerveless means no veins. It is often used for veins that are not visible, so absence may be too strong.
Sheathless means no leaf sheath.
Rostellate means with a small beak. The 'small' is lost but the meaning is kept.
Acrescent is a variant spelling of accrescent.
Isophyllous means the leaves on a shoot are alike. The target covers size only, not shape.
Uniserial is a synonym of uniseriate.
Cleft means cut about halfway, which is palmatifid, a subclass of palmately lobed. Palmately lobed loses the depth.
Dimidiate means halved, with one side missing or undeveloped. Asymmetrical fits roughly.
Lucid means shining. It can also be read as translucent.
Albuminous seeds have endosperm (albumen).
A thorn-tipped apex is spine-tipped.
Capillaceous means hair-like, which is filiform.
Superimposed buds or parts sit one above another, which is stacked.
Colliculate means with small hill-like bumps. Tuberculate is wart-like, which is close but not exact.
Negation of secund.
Not overlapping means not imbricate.
Headlike means capitate.
Negation of ciliated.
Nervose means conspicuously veined, not just having veins. Vascular bundle present loses the 'prominent'. Consider rejecting.
Long-ovate means elongate ovate, and ovate loses the elongation. Ovate-oblong is a different shape.
A sod-forming plant makes dense turf or mats.
A net-like pattern of pits matches alveolate.
Prominent loses the convex shape of the raised part.
Band-shaped is strap-shaped.
Glomerular means in tight clusters (glomerules), which is aggregated.
Non-ciliate means not ciliated.
Gracile means slender.
Laxly means loosely.
Veins described as connected are joined into a network. The constraint limits this to veins.
Buff is a pale yellowish brown.
Taproot is a synonym of primary root.
A drip tip is a narrowly drawn-out tail-like apex.
Semievergreen is the same as semi-deciduous.
Liguliform means strap-shaped.
Well spaced means evenly spaced, not widely separated. Distant means far apart. Reject the rule.
Insignificant means inconspicuous only for showy parts. For other parts it can simply mean small.
Negation of ruminate.
Linear-elongate is a long linear shape.
Not compressed means not flattened.
Erect-patent means spreading upward, which is close to ascending.
Hyaline is a synonym of transparent in PATO, so the negation fits.
Glandular hairs are glandular trichomes. 'Without' means they are absent.
Tussocky means growing in tussocks, which is the caespitose habit.
Aristulate means bearing a small awn, so an awn is present. The 'small' is lost, but it is minor.
Hooded is cucullate, so 'not hooded' is not cucullate.
Plain negation of undulate.
Plain negation of flattened.
Domatia are absent.
'Expanding' usually describes growth or unfolding in time, as in 'expanding leaves'. It does not mean dilated. Reject the word.
Bristles are only one kind of trichome. Bristleless does not mean there are no trichomes at all. The target needs 'bristle absent'.
Thickened maps to increased thickness. 'Evenly' only describes how the thickening is distributed.
Perulate means having perulae (bud scales), so they are present.
Isostylous means the styles are all of the same length, so the flower is not heterostylous.
Infertile is sterile.
Squamulose means covered with small scales, which is a kind of scaly.
'Not produced' is a generic phrase, for example 'not produced beyond the apex'. It does not mean not excurrent. Reject the word.
Bigeniculate means bent twice (a twice-kneed awn). 'Bent' loses the 'twice'.
Articulate means jointed, so non-articulate is not jointed.
Crater-like means bowl or cup shaped with a depression.
Bulbiferous means bearing bulbils.
Semilunate means half-moon shaped, which is crescent-shaped.
On leaves, stems and hairs, harsh means rough to the touch, which is scabrous. The constraint is already set.
'Long' is lost. A long awn is more specific than an awn being present. Map to awn present plus a length value, or reject.
Plain negation of recurved.
Palmatinerved means palmate venation, with several primary veins from the base. That is actinodromous.
Well-marked means distinct or conspicuous.
Not apparent means hardly visible, which is inconspicuous.
Tussock-forming is the caespitose habit.
Tiered means arranged in layers or storeys, which is stratified.
Quilted means puckered between the veins, which is bullate.
Tinted purple means purplish. The mapping to purple matches the usual handling of -ish and tinted colours.
Setuliferous means bearing small bristles, which is close to setose.
Bladder-like means inflated.
Not showy means inconspicuous.
Deltate is triangular. 'Broadly' is a degree modifier and is usually dropped.
Negation of resupinate, and the target is already a negated value class.
Semitransparent is partly transparent, which is translucent.
Densely set means crowded.
Striate-veined says the veins form fine parallel lines. 'Striated' alone loses the link to venation. Better 'veins striate' on the vein bearer, or reject.
Asperous means rough, which is scabrous.
Sharply tipped means the tip is pointed.
Same as 'well-marked'.
Rigid maps to inflexible, so the negation is not inflexible.
Plain negation of accrescent.
Rubbery means springy and elastic. This is a loose match for texture.
Aristate means bearing an awn, so 'not aristate' means the awn is absent.
Sclerotic means hardened.
Ampulliform means flask-shaped.
Flocculent means woolly or tufted, which is floccose.
Cap-shaped is dome-like, which is close to domed.
Parallel-nerved means the veins run parallel, which is parallelodromous.
Tuber-like means thickened and swollen like a tuber, which is the definition of tuberous.
Bicoloured is a case of multi-colored. The count of two is lost, but the parent class is safe.
Crown-shaped means crown like.
Slimy means mucoid.
Semiscandent means partly climbing or scrambling. The existing climbing and scrambling mapping already treats these as one habit.
Lunulate means crescent-shaped.
Semi-exserted means only partly projecting. Mapping it to exserted loses the 'partly'. Reject, or keep as a phrase for review.
Laminated means in thin layers, which fits stratified only for layered structures. On leaves it can mean lamina-like.
Lax-flowered means flowers loosely arranged on an inflorescence. The loose quality belongs to the inflorescence, and the bearer 'flower' is lost. Use inflorescence + loose, or reject.
Faveolate means honeycombed, the same as alveolate.
Defoliated means leafless, the leaves having been shed, so leaf absent describes the state.
Non-decurrent means not decurrent.
Ternately lobed means three-lobed.
The colour is brown and the comparative 'darker' only modifies it. Brown is a safe parent.
Acrid means pungent or burning, not bitter. Use a pungent class if one exists, otherwise reject.
Not reticulate negates reticulate.
Without prickles means prickle absent.
The colour is yellow and 'darker' only modifies it.
Epigeous means growing above ground, which is aerial.
Glomerule is a noun for a dense cluster of flowers, which is a bearer or inflorescence type. It is not the quality capitate. The quality form would be glomerate.
Exstipulate means without stipules.
Decreasing is ambiguous because it can mean size or number. Tapered size fits only for organs that get smaller along an axis.
'Divided almost' is a fragment of 'divided almost to the base'. The depth is lost, and the word on its own is not a quality. Reject, or handle as a phrase.
Scutelliform means shallow dish or shield shaped, which is close to saucer-shaped (patelliform).
Spatheless means without a spathe.
Not perforated means not perforate.
Non-anastomosing means not anastomosing.
Closely set means close to its neighbours, which matches the approximate definition.
Unwrinkled means not wrinkled.
Glossy is a synonym of glistening, so not glossy means not glistening.
Spotless means not spotted.
Spurlike means spur shaped.
Without bristles means not setose.
Flowerless means without flowers.
Marine means living in the sea, so salt water is lost. Aquatic is a parent term, but the rule needs a marine or saline class or manual review.
Lacinate is a spelling variant of laciniate.
In-rolled means rolled inward, which is involute.
Ovulate means female. The cone|strobilus constraint is right.
Ring-like means ring shaped.
Cincinnate describes an inflorescence or branching that is a cincinnus (scorpioid). It is not a presence of a separate part, so keep it to inflorescence-type bearers.
Interlaced means intertwined, which fits tangled.
Mammiform means breast or nipple shaped, which is close to papillary. It is not exact.
Not mucronate negates mucronate.
Ill-defined means indistinct or not sharply delimited, as with margins or limits. It does not mean inconspicuous (hard to see).
Not grooved negates grooved.
Knee-like means geniculate, or abruptly bent.
Ear-like means auriculate.
Leaf-bearing means the part has leaves.
Lipped means two-lipped. The constraint to corolla|calyx|perianth is right.
Edentate means without teeth, so not dentated.
Nipple-like (mammillate or papillate) fits papillary, though a papilla is smaller than a nipple.
Pilose means long soft hairs. Glandular-pubescent says short soft hairs plus glands, so the hair type is lost.
Ribbon-shaped and strap-shaped both mean long, narrow and parallel-sided.
Nonglandular means not glandular.
Striate-nerved means many fine parallel veins, which is parallel venation.
Ecarinate means without a keel, which fits not keel-shaped.
Radially symmetric is the same as actinomorphic.
Globoid means globe-like, which is spherical. PATO lists globular as a synonym.
Not carinate means not keeled.
Voluble means twining, which is a kind of climbing.
Juxtaposed means side by side and close together, which fits approximate.
Long-lived means a long life span. It applies to a plant or a leaf.
The negation of saccate (pouch-shaped) is mapped to the FLOPO saccate class.
Not persistent means falling off, which is deciduous.
Moderate-sized is the same as medium-sized.
Plan-convex is a spelling variant of plano-convex.
Glanduliferous means bearing glands, so a gland is present.
Cancellate means latticed, which is a reticulate pattern.
Rimose means cracked or chinked, which is fissured.
Not crisped is the negation of crisped.
Soldered means fused, which is connate.
Non-lenticellate means no lenticels.
Fully developed is the opposite of undeveloped or immature. It is not the opposite of vestigial. Do not map it.
Obloid is the solid form of oblong.
Exauriculate means without auricles.
Bracteal means of or like a bract.
Not tailed means not caudate.
The word 'long' (length of the sheath) is lost when this is mapped to plain sheathing.
Binate means in pairs.
The PO lexicon lists pseudobulb as a synonym of corm. A botanist would say an orchid pseudobulb is not a corm, so the match is only fair.
Beadlike means moniliform.
Buried means subterranean only for organs that sit in soil. 'Seeds buried in pulp' would be wrong.
Opposite to leaves is the same as leaf-opposed.
Tuberlike means like a tuber, which is tuberous.
Vittate means bearing vittae, so a vitta is present.
Embracing means clasping the stem, as amplexicaul does.
Goniautoicous is a kind of autoicous. This only holds for the whole moss plant, since the constraint says autoicous is not an organ sex.
Pseudopaniculate means falsely panicle-like.
Stipeless means no stipe (stalk), so the stalk is absent.
Without keel is treated like ecarinate. A 'keel absent' form would be a more exact target, but this is consistent with R0606.
Barbellulate means minutely barbellate. The small size is lost, but it is the same character.
Arilless means without an aril.
Pea-like means a pea-type (papilionaceous) flower or a pea-like fruit. It does not mean that a keel is present.
Not gland-dotted is the negation of gland-dotted.
Broomlike means many slender erect twigs. That is close to virgate, but only for the plant, stems and branches.
Not crested is the negation of crested.
Not veined means no veins, and PO lists vein as a synonym of vascular bundle.
Cleistocarpous means a capsule that does not open, which is not dehiscent.
Untwisted means not twisted.
Not splitting usually describes a fruit that does not open, which is not dehiscent. PATO 'split' means clefted, which is a different meaning.
Cirrose means bearing a tendril, which is what tendrilous means.
Caudiculate means having a caudicle, as in orchid pollinia.
'Low' makes the shape flat or shallow, a different form from plain conical.
Vinaceous means wine-coloured, which is close to reddish purple. This is an approximation. It could instead go to dark purplish red, as burgundy does.
Not disarticulating means the structure does not break apart at joints, and the negated 'jointed' value stands for that. I could not read the definition of FLOPO_0991154 to confirm.
Corneous means horny and hard. Hard keeps the main sense, though it loses the horn-like texture.
Lacerate is defined as an irregularly cut margin, as if torn. That matches irregularly incised.
Aseptate means without septa.
Multistratose means having many layers, which is stratified.
Rugulate means finely wrinkled. Rugose is the nearest PATO term.
The shape is still triangular. 'Long' only adds the proportion.
Cross-striolate means finely striped across the surface.
Setulose means bearing small bristles, which are stiff. Pubescent means soft hairs, so these are different indumentum types.
Inermes means unarmed, with no spines or prickles, which is 'not spiny'.
Unpleasantly scented is the definition of foetid.
Purple tinged means tinged with purple. It maps to the colour purple, and the 'tinged' degree is lost.
The word gives a count of veins. 'Vascular bundle present' loses the number and says nothing a veined part would not already say.
Paleate means bearing paleae, chaffy scales or bracts. The flower bract term lists chaff as a synonym.
Loop-connected veins are joined in loops, which is anastomosing.
This is a variant spelling of loculicidal.
Scant means few or sparse.
Stipellate means having stipels.
The word means erect and also pressed against the surface. Appressed alone loses 'erect'.
Racemoid means raceme-like.
Twisted is the synonym of torsioned, so 'not twisted' is its negation.
Bulged only means swollen or protruding. Gibbous means swollen on one side, which is narrower.
Checkered means a pattern of squares, which is tessellated.
Burgundy is a dark purplish red.
Spiculose means covered with small spicules, which are minute hard points. This is near muricate.
Converging means leaning toward each other. Connivent also says the parts touch without fusing, and the word 'converging' does not say that. Convergent would be the better target if one exists.
Nipple-shaped is mammillate or papillate, which is close to papillary.
Pocket-shaped means pouched, which is saccate.
Cormose means bearing a corm.
Compacted means condensed, and PATO lists compressed as a synonym of condensed.
Sward-forming means forming a dense turf, which is the same sense as mat-forming.
Deltoid means triangular, so the term is lanceolate-triangular.
Glomeruliform means in a dense cluster, which is aggregated.
Non-aristate means without an awn.
Elevated means raised above the surface, which is prominent. The negation carries over.
Obsolescent means nearly vanished or rudimentary, which is vestigial.
Assurgent means curving upward, which is ascending.
Stilt roots are prop roots.
Laticiferous means having latex-carrying cells (laticifers).
Domatiate means having domatia.
Bunched means clustered, and clustered is a synonym of aggregated.
Non-fibrous is the negation of fibrous.
Not fibrous is the negation of fibrous.
Not scarious is the negation of scarious.
Not stoloniferous means no stolons.
Forked means bifurcated, so the negation carries over.
Rhombic means rhomboid. The word 'broadly' is dropped, as in the other broad-X rules.
A pseudumbel is a false umbel, so umbel-shaped is acceptable. The word is a noun, so it is mostly a bearer shape.
'Mediocre' (French médiocre) means of middle size. The part constraint already limits it.
Pseudumbellate means umbel-like.
Etched veins are impressed or sunken lines, and the constraint limits the rule to veins.
Epappose means without a pappus, so absence of pappus is right.
Vernicose means varnished and shiny, which matches glistening (synonym glossy/shiny).
Gummy means exuding or covered with gum or resin. Viscid only means sticky and loses the gum.
'Sharply defined' describes a distinct margin or limit, not conspicuousness. It has no good existing target.
Bractiform means bract-shaped.
Dusky means dark and dull. PATO low brightness has the synonym dark.
Bilaterally compressed is the same as laterally compressed.
Sac-like means saccate.
The rule loses the round shape. Round-raised is a raised, rounded structure, and prominent says nothing about shape.
Not split means undivided.
Complicate means folded upon itself, as in leaves folded lengthwise.
Non-foliaceous means not leaf-like.
The negation of glandular is kept.
Striate means striated, and the negation is kept.
The FLOPO term lists 'spicy' as a synonym. Spicy can also mean a taste, but scent is the usual use in floras.
Antheriferous means bearing anthers.
Without tubercles means not tuberculate.
Aqueous means watery, for example sap or latex.
A frilled margin is ruffled or wavy, which is close to crisped. It is not the same as fringed.
Stomatose means bearing stomata.
Without auricles means not auriculate.
Suberous is the same as suberose, which is corky.
Nervous means with visible veins (nerves). This holds for flat parts, and PO lists vein as a synonym of vascular bundle. It is doubtful for other parts.
Semi-transparent means translucent.
Bean-like means kidney-shaped, which is reniform.
As a quality, thyrsus means a thyrse-like inflorescence.
The negation of auriculate is kept.
The negation of elongated is kept.
Pseudo-umbellate is the same as pseudumbellate.
Vestigial means a rudimentary remnant. Scarcely developed only means barely developed, which is weaker.
Parallel veined means parallelodromous venation.
Biparous (a biparous cyme) means two lateral branches under the terminal flower, a dichasium. It is not bifurcated.
Ruminated, as in ruminate endosperm, means ruminate.
Imperceptible means not noticeable, so inconspicuous.
Canaliculate means channelled or grooved.
Acutely angled means angular. The word 'acutely' is dropped.
The negation of connivent is kept.
Torulose is a mild moniliform. The negation is kept.
Sandpapery means rough, which is scabrous.
Broad-elliptic is elliptic. The word 'broad' is dropped.
Contorted means twisted, and torsioned has the synonym twisted.
Ovoid is a synonym of ovate in PATO. The word 'short' is dropped.
Tardily dehiscent still means dehiscent. Only the timing is lost.
Hamate means hooked, which is a synonym of falciform in PATO.
The negation of tuberous is kept.
'Pale' is lost. Chestnut colour alone is not pale chestnut-brown.
Foliated means bearing leaves, which is the same as leafy.
Orthotropic means growing vertically. The constraint to stem, shoot system and branch is right.
A syncarpous fruit has fused carpels, and the fruit constraint is already there. Syncarp can also mean a multiple fruit, so this is not certain.
Hypocrepiform means horseshoe-shaped. Salverform is hypocrateriform, a different word. No class for the right shape was found.
A collar-like part forms a ring around something, so ring shaped fits.
Not fused means free.
Without colleters means colleter absent.
The target is a leaf midvein. On a sepal, bract or petal the midrib is not a leaf midvein.
Supra-axillary means above the axil. Extra-axillary only means outside the axil, so the position is lost.
Furry means covered with soft hairs, so hairy fits.
Immaculate means without spots, so not spotted fits.
Pointed is the general class that includes a long-apiculate tip. Some detail is lost but nothing false is said.
The calyx is made of sepals, so calyx-like means sepal-like.
Lamellose means with thin plate-like ridges, so ridged fits roughly.
Not flaring means not flared.
Huge is a large size, so increased size fits.
The arcuate (curved) form of the ascent is lost. The curved form would need a second quality.
Long-tailed means caudate.
Not glabrous is the negation of glabrous.
Unthickened means not thickened.
Columellate is a pollen exine term (rod-like columellae). PO columella is a different structure, for example the moss capsule columella.
Endospermless means endosperm absent.
Declining means bent or directed downward, which is close to descending.
Reticulate is lost. The word means a net pattern with pits, so it needs both reticulate and alveolate.
Weakly defined means indistinct, so inconspicuous fits.
Directed forward means pointing toward the apex, which is antrorse.
Excised means cut out, not a notched apex. Emarginate is a specific shape of a tip and the two are not the same.
Honeycomb-like means alveolate.
Packed means crowded.
A running rhizome, rootstock or stolon is a creeping one. The constraint is right.
Tattered means irregularly torn, which is lacerate.
Virgately branched means with wand-like branches, which is virgate.
Psilate means smooth, mostly used for pollen and seeds.
Tail-like means caudate.
Accuminate is a misspelling of acuminate.
Lozenge-shaped means rhomboid.
Not broadened is the negation of dilated or expanded. The match is rough.
Not connate is the negation of connate.
Not spine-tipped is the negation of spine-tipped.
Pimpled means with small bumps, which is papillose.
Pitless means not pitted, which is not foveate.
A pseudoraceme is a raceme-like inflorescence.
Gland-covered means the part carries glands. The 'covered' (many glands) part is lost, but the gland is there.
Equal-sized means equal.
Interlacing veins form a net, which is reticulate. It could also mean anastomosing.
The bearer (nerves or veins) is lost. The meaning is that the venation is inconspicuous, so it needs the nerve or vein as bearer.
Not septate means septum absent.
Ear-shaped means auriculate.
Without buttresses means not buttressed.
Distorted means misshapen, which is what deformed means.
A fig-shaped structure is pear-shaped (obovoid and narrowed to the base).
Narrow-necked only says the neck is narrow. Flask-shaped also says the body is swollen below, and that is not stated.
Petiolelike means resembling a petiole or stalk. Attenuate means tapering gradually to a point, which is a different thing.
Scarcely distinct (veins, margins and the like) means hardly visible, which is inconspicuous.
Single-rowed means uniseriate.
The bare word tearing does not mean fragile. It can describe how a part splits or opens, or the action of tearing. Fragile needs an explicit statement such as breaking easily.
A carrot-like part, usually a root, is conical and tapering.
A collar is a ring around an axis, so collar-shaped means ring shaped.
Covered with bristles means setose.
Drawn out (into a tip or point) is the same as attenuate.
Knob-shaped can describe a swelling anywhere on a part. Head-shaped is defined as abruptly enlarged at the tip into a rounded head.
Nodule-bearing means root nodules for roots. Leaf and stem nodules also occur, for example bacterial leaf nodules in Psychotria, so the rule should not apply to other parts.
Pulviniform means cushion-shaped, which is pulvinate.
Lenticelless means without lenticels, an absence of the lenticel entity.
Persisting for a long time means not falling off, which is non-deciduous. The word long is lost, but that is acceptable.
A maple-like leaf is palmately lobed. The leaf constraint is right.
A semi-shrub is a suffrutescent plant, and the whole-plant constraint is right.
Broom-like means many slender erect twigs, as in a broom. Virgate means wand-like, which is long, slender, straight and erect.
The rule loses the position (centrally). The statement says only that the part is not constricted in the middle.
Trigone is a variant of trigonous (three-angled).
Awn-tipped means an awn is present at the tip.
Thinly textured means thin in texture, which is decreased thickness.
Pinninerved means pinnately veined.
Rolled under (margins) means revolute.
Thin-coriaceous means somewhat leathery, which is subcoriaceous.
Pilulose is not a clear synonym of puberulous. It is rare and can mean bearing small ball-like bodies, so the mapping is doubtful.
Stegocarpic moss capsules have an operculum (lid), so presence of the operculum is right.
Flexuous means wavy or zigzag, which is sinuous, so not flexuous is not sinuous.
Without keels says the keel structure is missing. It does not say the shape is not keel-shaped. This should be an entity-absence rule, not a negated shape.
Lanuginous means woolly, which is lanate.
A bunchgrass grows in tufts, which is caespitose.
Lophate means crested or ridged. Ridged is the nearest term.
Inermous means unarmed, with no spines or prickles, so not spiny is right.
Keelless means no keel. It does not mean not keel-shaped, so it should be an absence rule.
Paniclelike means panicle-like.
Racemelike means raceme-like.
Exalbuminous means the seed has no albumen (endosperm).
Thickly textured means thick, which is increased thickness.
Rampant means vigorous and spreading unchecked. It does not mean creeping along the ground.
Biserial means in two rows, which is biseriate.
Delimited means bounded or marked off by a limit. It does not mean conspicuous.
Hoodlike means cucullate.
Not imbricate is the negation of imbricate.
Nigrescent means turning black or blackish. Black loses the becoming or tending part.
Pubescent-glandular is the same as glandular-pubescent, with the word order swapped.
Estipitate means without a stipe, so not stipitate.
Sheathed can mean enclosed by a sheath. Sheathing means wrapping round an axis. Not sheathed does not clearly negate the wrapping quality.
Shreddy normally describes bark that peels in shreds. The exfoliating term is for bark and axes, not other parts.
Linear-reticulate means marked with a network, which is reticulate. The linear detail is lost, but that is minor.
Bracted means bracts are present.
Multicipital means many-headed, with a stem base or caudex that branches into many heads. It is not branching in general.
Subnull means almost absent or very reduced, which fits vestigial.
Cannelled means channelled or grooved, which is furrowed.
Rosetted is the same as rosulate.
Hemicylindrical is half-cylindrical, flat on one side and round on the other. This matches plano-convex.
Epedunculate means without a peduncle.
Nodose means knobby or knotty, so non-nodose is not knobbled.
Thinned can mean made thin, but it can also mean reduced in density or number. It only means decreased thickness for plain parts.
Prophyllate means a prophyll is present.
The word includes its bearer, the stem. A rule on decreased strength alone loses that the stem is the weak part. It should be stem + decreased strength.
Bosselated means covered in rounded bosses or knobs, which is knobbled.
Daisy-like means radiate only for composite heads or flowers.
Pliant means flexible.
Hoodlike means cucullate, so not hoodlike is not cucullate.
Pennate means pinnately veined only on a blade or leaflet. On a whole leaf it often means pinnate, with leaflets.
Hooked is a listed synonym of falciform.
Multiveined means many veins, which is a count. 'Vascular bundle present' loses the 'many'. It should not be mapped without the count.
Epapillose means without papillae, which is not papillose.
Non-acrescent is not accrescent.
The French bosselée means bossed or knobbly, which is knobbled.
Netlike is reticulate.
Plate-shaped is platelike, a listed synonym.
Long-rhomboidal means elongate rhombic. Rhomboid alone loses the elongation.
Deep-seated means subterranean only for underground organs. Other parts, such as glands or veins, can also be deep-seated.
Graceful is an aesthetic word and does not mean slender. No safe target exists.
The French caduc means falling off or deciduous.
Minuscule means very small, which is decreased size.
Cyathiforme means cup-shaped.
Bucciniform means trumpet-shaped.
Pinnately cleft is the same as pinnatifid.
Subspheric is subspherical.
Auricles also occur on leaf blades, not only on the sheath, so this is only right for grass-like leaves. The part must be a leaf or sheath.
Matlike means forming mats.
Hirtellous means finely and shortly hairy, so glandular-pubescent is close. Some detail is lost.
Tuft-forming means tufted, which is caespitose.
Unequally sided means asymmetrical, as in leaf bases.
Corky-thickened means thickened with cork. Corky keeps the main meaning.
Stalked glands are stipitate glands, so this is not stipitate-glandular.
Pale-speckled adds a pale colour of the spots. Spotted alone loses it.
Mutic means without an awn or point, and it is used for grass parts. On other parts it can mean having no mucro or spine.
Sarmentous means with long, slender, trailing or runner-like stems. That is not always climbing.
Linear-foveolate means small pits in a linear arrangement. Foveate loses the linear arrangement.
Trichome-tufted means hairs in tufts, which is close to bearded.
Without tufts of hairs is not bearded.
Hood-forming is cucullate.
Paniculoid means panicle-like.
Anthela is an inflorescence type. The word as a quality means an anthela is present.
Biramous means two-branched, which is bifurcated.
Bright is a listed synonym of high saturation.
Applanate means flattened.
Bearing glochids means glochids are present. FLOPO_0986043 is the glochid class in the anatomy registry.
Pencil-like means a slender cylinder.
Rectilinear means straight.
The verb form of anastomosing. Both are used for veins and other branches that join.
Oppositifolius means opposite a leaf, so leaf-opposed.
Pulpous means pulpy, which is fleshy.
Plane-convex is a spelling variant of plano-convex.
Radicant means rooting from the stem, which is shoot-borne roots present. The PO synonym list includes adventitious root.
Aerenchymatous means having aerenchyma.
Moundlike means a rounded mound, which is domed.
A falsely petiolate leaf has a narrowed base that looks like a petiole (a pseudopetiole). It does not mean the whole leaf tapers. Leave it unmapped or reject it.
Semispherical means hemispherical.
Gland is a synonym of this PO class, so without glands means glands absent.
Recumbent means lying on the ground. With the part constraint (plant, stem, branch) it is close to prostrate.
French soudés means fused, which is connate for parts of the same kind. It can mean adnate for parts of different kinds, but connate is the usual reading.
Panicked is a variant of panicled, meaning arranged in a panicle.
Voluminous means bulky, which is increased volume. It is vague, so confidence is moderate.
A misspelling of pedunculate.
Lanulose means finely woolly. Lanate is the nearest class, and only the diminutive sense is lost.
Vinelike means growing like a vine, which is climbing. It is in the same habit group as scandent.
The plain negation of beaked.
Uncolored means colorless.
Conchiform means shell-shaped.
Ramose means branched.
Broadly orbicular is still orbicular. Only the degree of breadth is lost, which a rule can accept.
Geocarpic means the fruit ripens underground, so it only applies to fruiting parts. Subterranean is the closest class for them.
The plain negation of adherent.
Eporose means without pores. Pores are not the same as perforations (perforate), so not perforate loses the meaning. Pore absence on the bearer is more exact.
Limbless fits leaf lamina absent only for leaf-like parts. For petals or a corolla, limb means something else.
Short-oval means a short ellipse, which is close to broadly elliptic. Only the ratio is lost.
French sacciforme means sac-shaped, which is saccate.
Trihedral means three-angled, which is trigonous in cross-section.
Diminished means reduced in size.
Even-sized means equal in size.
Limp means lacking stiffness, which is flexible. The plain reading fits.
A misspelling of pedicellate.
Villoso-ciliate means villous and ciliate. Mapping to ciliated alone loses the villous hairs. Split it into two qualities, or leave it unmapped.
The negation of foliaceous (leaf-like).
Coarsely serrate is still serrate. Only the degree is lost.
Blond means pale yellowish, and straw yellow is the nearest class. Confidence is moderate.
The PATO synonym needle-like is on subulate. Acicular would be the exact term, but subulate is close.
Thick-papery is the papery or chartaceous texture. Only the thickness is lost.
Closely arranged means approximate, in the sense of close together.
Interconnected means anastomosing only for veins and similar networks. For other parts it just means connected.
Lactiferous means bearing latex, which is laticifers present. The class is the cell that makes latex.
Rhombiform means rhomboid.
Narrowly cylindrical is still cylindrical. Only the degree is lost.
Eligulate means without a ligule.
The negation of nodose, which is knobbled.
Scattered describes how things are arranged. Sparse describes how few there are. The two are not the same.
Sloping means sloped.
Functionally staminate means the flower has some female parts but acts as male. Plain 'male' loses the word 'functionally'.
Scattered-pilose means sparsely hairy. Plain pilose loses the sparse density.
Tongue-like means ligulate, which is strap-shaped.
Pseudoumbellate means looking like an umbel.
Pinniveined means pinnately veined.
Slightly raised is close enough to prominent. The 'slightly' is lost.
Canoe-shaped means boat-shaped, which is scaphoid.
Bloom is the waxy coating that makes a surface glaucous.
Crustose means crust-like and hard. This is close enough to crustaceous.
Dehiscence is the process or the mode of opening. It does not say the part is dehiscent. It can come with 'indehiscent' or 'by slits'.
Inermis means unarmed, which is not spiny.
Same word with the hyphen removed.
Crater-shaped is crateriform, a wide bowl or cup.
Gutter-shaped is channelled, which is grooved.
The target is the secondary vein of a leaf. Other parts such as petals or bracts also have lateral veins.
Increasing is generic, for example in size or number. Accrescent means a part that keeps growing after flowering, such as the calyx.
Not persisting means falling off, which is deciduous.
Tuberiform means tuber-like, which is tuberous.
Farina is a mealy powder.
Disclike is a synonym of discoid.
Same meaning.
Pointless means without a point.
Dagger-shaped is close to blade-like or sword-shaped.
Gibbose is a variant spelling of gibbous.
Densely clothed means densely covered with hairs or indumentum. Plain dense loses what covers the surface.
Tooth-shaped means dentiform. It is not necessarily triangular.
Irregularly quadrate is not a regular square. The 'irregularly' is lost.
Leaflet-like means resembling a small leaf, which is leaf-like.
Rufescent means reddish brown.
Short-rostrate means short-beaked. The 'short' is lost.
Fragmenting means breaking into pieces.
Tinged with pink is a pink colour. The weaker intensity is lost.
Epapillate means without papillae.
Short-stalked glandular hairs are still stipitate-glandular.
Closely placed means approximate.
Darker pink is still pink.
Lustrous means glistening, so the negation fits.
Obcordiform is the same as obcordate.
Tinged brown is a brown colour. The weaker intensity is lost.
Squamulate means with small scales.
The part constraint limits it to hard coverings, which fits crustaceous.
Covered with sporangia means sporangia are present.
Loriform means strap-shaped.
Leaf-scarred means leaf scars are present.
Lenticel as a descriptive word means lenticels are present.
Semi-globular means hemispherical.
Bract-covered means bracts are present.
Same meaning.
Anther-bearing means anthers are present on the part. Anther is PO_0009066 in the lexicon.
Gamosépale means the sepals are fused, which is connate.
Alveolar means honeycomb-pitted, which is alveolate.
Lagéniforme is French for flask-shaped.
Pseudo-axillary means only apparently axillary, not truly axillary. Extra-axillary means outside the axil, and the 'apparently' is lost. Keep the rule only if no better term exists.
Silloned is an English-text form of the French sillonné (furrowed), which is sulcate.
Cerebriform means brain-like with convoluted ridges. Rugose is the closest existing term and a new term is not worth it.
Glandular-tipped describes hairs with a gland at the tip. That is stipitate-glandular, not a glandular-pubescent indumentum.
Costulate means having small ribs, so ribbed fits.
Reticulate-nerved means the veins form a net, which is reticulate venation.
'Midvein extending' is ambiguous. It may extend beyond the apex (excurrent) or only to it. Percurrent means to the apex and not beyond, so this rule over-commits.
Checked bark is cracked into small blocks, which fits fissured (cracked).
Guttered means channelled or grooved.
Clustered is a synonym of aggregated, so the negation is fine.
Direct negation of rugose.
PO_0004544 has 'sucker' as a synonym, so not suckering means suckers are absent. Not suckering describes behaviour, which is a slightly looser reading.
PO_0025172 is thorn, so 'without thorns' means thorn absent.
Satiny means a soft sheen, and glistening (glossy, shiny) is the closest existing term.
Surculose means bearing suckers, and sucker is a synonym of PO_0004544.
Inodorous means without odour.
Channeled is a synonym of grooved, so the negation is fine.
Obcuneiform means inversely wedge-shaped, with the narrow end at the apex. Cuneate loses the 'ob-' and so reverses the orientation. Better as a new term, or reject.
Strangulate means abruptly constricted.
Vining is a climbing habit.
Gland-tipped hairs are glandular trichomes, so 'without' means they are absent.
Easily broken is brittle.
Hardly thickened means essentially not thickened.
Geniculate means sharply bent like a knee. 'Not geniculate' may still be curved or bent, so 'not bent' is too strong.
Direct negation of spreading.
Stalkless means sessile.
Tinged purple means faintly or partly purple. Purple loses the 'slightly' meaning.
Defined means distinct or clearly delimited, such as a defined margin. It does not mean conspicuous.
Semi-annular means half-ring, which is crescent-shaped.
Cirriform means tendril-like.
Pits holding glands are close to gland-dotted. No better existing term.
A long-tipped apex is acuminate (drawn out into a long point).
'Not clearly differentiated' means not distinct from a neighbouring part, for example calyx and corolla. It is not about conspicuousness.
Sheath-less means the sheath is missing, so the entity is absent. 'Not sheathing' means the part does not clasp, which is a different claim. Use sheath absent.
Stigmatose means having a stigma.
A trailer is a trailing, prostrate plant.
Tuft-like clusters are fascicled.
Defoliate means the leaves have been shed, which is a state or time-bound loss. It does not mean leaves are absent. Better as deciduous or leafless-at-time, or reject.
Radiculose means bearing rootlets or rhizoids, so the negation is rhizoid absent.
Compound corymb is a specific kind of inflorescence. Plain 'corymb present' loses 'compound'. Constrain it or leave unmapped.
A tendril-tipped rachis only exists on compound leaves. On a simple leaf the tendril is at the apex of the lamina.
Unisex is unisexual.
Variable-sized means size differs among individuals or samples. Unequal means parts differ within one structure. These are different characters.
Junciform means rush-like, which is slender and terete. Terete is the closest existing term.
Sillonné is French for furrowed or grooved.
Soudées is French for fused, which is connate.
A flared base means buttressed only for trees and trunks. On other parts it is not a buttress.
'Very acute' is acute. The intensity word is lost, which is minor.
'Fascicle-like' means fascicled.
Two-ranked is the plain-English term for distichous.
Ceriferous means wax-bearing, so waxy.
The bare word 'lenticels' used as a quality means lenticels are present. I did not check that PO_0000031 is lenticel.
Single-celled hairs, glands and papillae are unicellular. The constraint is already correct.
Elongate-obovate is obovate and elongate. The 'elongate' part is lost, which is minor.
Fornicate means arched or vaulted.
Light buff is a pale yellowish brown. Light brown is the nearest PATO colour.
Crusty means crust-like, which is crustaceous.
Globe-shaped is spherical.
Glandular papillate means papillae that are glandular. Mapping to papillose alone loses 'glandular'.
'Not barbed' is the negation of barbed.
'Not filiform' is the negation of filiform.
Inrolled means involute, so 'not inrolled' is 'not involute'.
Pleasant is a judgement of scent, not sweetness. A pleasant scent need not be sweet. The flower constraint also does not restrict it to scent.
Sharp-angled means angular.
Stomate-bearing means stomata are present. I did not check that PO_0002000 is the stomatal complex.
'Base cuneate' is cuneate. The part word is redundant.
Blocky (bark in blocks) is not tessellated (checkered). Reject rather than guess.
Granular-papillose is a papillose surface. The 'granular' part is lost, which is minor.
Grooveless means not grooved.
Mounded means heaped or dome-like. Pulvinate means cushion-shaped, or a swollen leaf base.
Funnelform is funnel-shaped. 'Narrowly' is lost, which is minor.
Phaneroporous stomata are exposed at the surface, not sunken. Cryptoporous is the sunken kind.
Pungent-tipped means ending in a stiff sharp point or spine.
The veins are rugose, not the whole part. Plain rugose puts the wrinkling on the whole surface.
Setaceous-tipped means the tip is bristle-like. It does not mean a true awn is present.
Incised is a synonym of cut. 'Shallowly' is lost, which is minor.
'Shortly rectangular' is rectangular.
Unconstricted means not constricted.
Unmottled means not mottled.
A violet scent is a sweet scent. The specific scent is lost, which is minor.
'Without rhizomes' means rhizome absent.
Bracteose means bearing bracts.
Clumped is a synonym of aggregated.
Narrow-rectangular is rectangular.
'Not fleshy' is the negation of fleshy.
'Not lenticellate' means lenticels are absent. I did not check that PO_0000031 is lenticel.
Rounded rectangular is rectangular with rounded corners.
Subpatent means slightly spreading. Patent means spreading.
Subuliform means awl-shaped, which is subulate.
Pitted means the glands sit in pits. Gland-dotted only means glands show as dots.
Knee-shaped means abruptly bent (geniculate).
United parts are connate. 'Partially' is lost, which is minor.
Pore-bearing means having pores. Perforate is the nearest term.
Recessed means sunken.
Styliferous means bearing a style.
A vanilla scent is a sweet scent. The specific scent is lost, which is minor.
'Disagreeable' in floras nearly always means an offensive smell, which is what foetid covers.
Rosette-like means arranged in a dense radiating cluster on a short axis, which is the definition of rosulate.
The negation of sheathing is correct.
The word says the streaks are dark green. The rule keeps only 'streaked' and drops the colour. Map it to streaked plus dark green, or reject it.
Porate anthers open by pores, which is poricidal. The constraint to anther or synandrium avoids pollen porate, which is a different thing.
Quilted-sunken describes a puckered or bullate surface with sunken veins. Plain 'sunken' loses the quilted pattern.
The hairs surround another organ. The rule asserts only that the bearer has trichomes, and the word never names the bearer, so the meaning is lost.
'Applied' (French appliqué) means pressed flat against a surface, which is appressed.
Claviforme is a synonym of clavate (club-shaped).
Glomerule-like means in small, dense, rounded clusters. 'Condensed' does not carry the head-like or cluster shape.
Isomorphous means the structures have the same form. That is not the same as 'not dimorphic', because they could still be trimorphic. Reject it.
The negation of imbricate is correct.
French sillonné means furrowed or grooved, which is sulcate.
Synandrous means the anthers or stamens are united (connate). The bearer constraint is appropriate.
'Weakly marked' means faint, and it fits inconspicuous only for lines, veins and markings. It does not fit parts in general.
The word 'aril' as a descriptor means an aril is present.
The brown colour is lost. Banded alone does not say what colour the stripes are.
Caulinar is a variant spelling of cauline.
Laciniated is the same as laciniate.
'Not looped' covers any venation without loops (for example craspedodromous or parallel). It does not mean 'not brochidodromous'.
High-climbing describes climbing plants such as lianas.
Same meaning as the target.
Midribless means the leaf has no midrib or midvein.
Pseudopedicellate means falsely stalked, with a stalk-like base that is not a true pedicel. Stipitate is a different kind of stalk.
Scimitar-shaped is sickle-shaped, and falciform lists scythe-shaped, sickle-shaped and falcate as synonyms.
'Darker orange' is a comparison with something else, so it does not state an absolute dark orange.
Lenticillate is a misspelling of lenticellate, which means bearing lenticels.
The brown colour is lost. Spotted alone does not say what colour the flecks are.
A strong smell is an increased odour.
Wine-coloured means dark red, sometimes purplish red.
Bundled means borne in a close cluster, which is fascicled.
Ciliate-hairy means fringed with cilia (marginal hairs).
Cirrate means bearing a cirrus (tendril). It does not mean curled.
'Coarsely divided' means dissected into broad segments, so the target still holds.
Deflected means bent away from the usual direction, which is bent.
'Evenly arranged' means a regular spacing pattern.
Forward-directed is the plain-English form of antrorse.
For a whole plant, free-standing means self-supporting, so not climbing. For parts, 'free' means not fused, which is a different meaning.
Glanduliform means gland-shaped. It does not mean the structure is glandular.
Long hairs that are soft and scattered fit the pilose definition.
The shape is rhomboid. 'Narrowly' only gives its proportions.
'Non-flowering' is said of shoots or plants that bear no flowers. It does not fit other parts.
The negation is correct.
Dentate is a label of the target class, so 'not dentate' means not dentated.
The negation of leafy is correct.
Toothed is a synonym of dentated.
Variegated is a synonym of multi-colored, so the negation is correct.
The negation of white is correct.
Penicellate is a misspelling of penicillate, which means brush-like.
Perennating describes organs (rhizome, bulb, bud) that survive the unfavourable season. It does not say the plant has a perennial life span.
Prickle-free means no prickles.
Rank-smelling means foul-smelling, which is foetid.
Satin-like means a soft silky sheen. Glistening means sparkling or shining, so the soft-sheen meaning is lost.
Scoop-shaped is a synonym for spoon-shaped.
Semi-translucent means only partly translucent. The degree is lost.
Slanting means oblique.
Stomateless means no stomata.
Strong-scented means increased odour.
Tortuose means twisted and winding, which is close to sinuous.
Spinules are small spines, so without spinules means not spiny.
Without stomata means stomata are absent.
Basally joined is basally connate. The basal position is lost, but the meaning is otherwise connate.
Close-set means placed close together, which is approximate.
Dark cherry red is a dark red.
Equal-length means the lengths are equal.
Equally wide means equal widths when two parts are compared, or the same width throughout. It does not mean parallel-sided.
Flesh-coloured means pale pinkish.
Lateral veins are secondary leaf veins only on leaves. Bracts, petals and other parts have lateral veins that are not PO secondary leaf veins.
Laxly spaced means distant.
Lighter coloured is a comparison of colour. It does not mean discolorous, which is two surfaces of different colour. Reject it.
Marked with leaf scars means leaf scars are present.
Nearly free means not quite free. The partial union is lost.
Not deflexed (not bent downward) does not mean not reflexed (not bent backward). The two terms are different.
Pedatifid means pedately cleft, which is close to pedate.
Spoon-like means spoon-shaped.
Stellately arranged describes an arrangement of parts radiating like a star. It is not the shape of a single part.
Stocky means short and sturdy, which is close to robust.
Water-repellent means hydrophobic.
Water-shedding often describes a shape, such as a drip tip, that sheds water. It is not necessarily a hydrophobic surface.
With domatia means domatia are present.
Without clearly defined stereids means they are indistinct. It does not mean they are absent.
Bunch-forming means tufted, which is caespitose.
Inarticulate means not jointed.
Narrowly foliose means narrowly leaf-like. The narrowness is lost.
Non-stoloniferous means no stolons.
Powdered means covered in powder, which is close to mealy.
Refuse is an ordinary English word (waste), so the rule is unsafe. Any retuse reading would be a guess at a typo.
PO lists utricle as a synonym of this class. Botanically a utricle is indehiscent, but it is close enough.
Degraded can mean decayed or worn. It does not mean vestigial, which is a reduced organ.
Densely placed means crowded.
Narrowly cylindric is cylindrical in shape.
Broader above the middle is the definition of obovate.
Naviculiform means boat-shaped, which is scaphoid.
PO lists siliqua as a synonym of silique.
Slightly widened loses the small degree. It is also only increased relative to something else.
Unawned means no awns.
Untoothed means not toothed.
Alternately long and short means unequal.
Gynandrous means stamens joined with the pistil, as in orchids. Androgynous means male and female flowers together. The two are different.
Late-dehiscent means opening late. The timing is lost, and a plain dehiscent value would be wrong for it.
Non-ruminated means the endosperm is smooth, not ruminate. The target is the negation of the ruminate value. I could not find FLOPO_0991205 in the value-term file, so I did not check it.
Not cordate means not heart-shaped.
A pseudo-umbel is an umbel-like inflorescence. The match is loose but acceptable.
Septicide is the noun form of septicidal, a capsule dehiscence type.
This is a narrow width. The 'very' only adds degree, which the broader target drops.
The smell is apple-like, and 'odorous' loses that. Map it to odorous only if the smell type is kept as a separate value.
Blanched means made white or pale, so 'white' is the nearest colour.
Densely foliated means leafy. The density is lost, but this is the usual handling of degree words.
Intertwined is the same as tangled.
Irregularly distributed is an irregular spatial pattern.
Left-twining gives the direction of twining (sinistrorse). 'Climbing' loses the direction. Use a twining or direction value if one exists.
The negation of notched.
Penninervous means pinnately veined.
Poorly visible means inconspicuous.
Saucer-like is saucer-shaped.
Finely ridged is ridged. The 'finely' is a degree word that gets dropped.
Incrusted means covered with a crust. The crust is not necessarily calcium, so 'calcified' adds a claim the word does not make.
Non-sticky means non-adhesive.
Antler-like describes a particular branching shape. 'Branched' loses the shape. Reject it or use a shape term.
Perceptible means can be detected. It does not mean conspicuous, which means easily seen.
Shortly spaced means closely spaced, which is crowded.
Subglobular is nearly spherical.
Enormous means a greatly increased size.
A false raceme (pseudoraceme) is a raceme-like inflorescence.
Tuber-forming means tubers are present.
Digitately nerved means several main veins radiate from one point, which is actinodromous.
The word means wavy-woolly. 'Lanate' loses the wavy part of the hair form.
Subvaginate means somewhat sheathing. That is not the same as clasping (amplexicaul), so the target loses the sheath.
The word is a mix of racemose and umbellate. 'Umbelliform' loses the racemose half.
Aporose means without pores, which is imperforate.
This is a loose match to leaf-like, since a leaflet is a leaf part.
A forb is a growth form, a non-grass herb. 'Herbaceous' loses the exclusion of grasses.
Ringlike is ring-shaped.
Caliculate means having an epicalyx.
Efibrillose means without fibrils.
Summer-green plants lose their leaves in the cold season, so this is deciduous.
Cannelé means grooved or fluted, which is furrowed.
Rugate is a variant of rugose.
The word is a mix of cymose and corymbose. 'Corymb-like' loses the cymose half.
Explanate means spread out flat.
The teeth are callose, meaning tipped with a hard callus. 'Dentated' loses the callose and the fineness of denticulate.
Floppy means limp, which is flexible.
Resinous-dotted means dotted with resin glands, which is gland-dotted.
'Neutral' means sexless or sterile only for florets and flowers. For other parts it is ambiguous, for example pH or colour.
Funiculate means having a funicle.
Fawny is a yellowish brown.
Short-tipped is a general description. It does not mean mucronulate, which is a specific small point.
Coniform is cone-shaped.
On these parts, 'falling' means falling off early (caducous), which is deciduous. The constraint already limits it to those parts.
On an involucre, not calyculate means no calyculus (outer small bracts), so epicalyx absent is a fair match.
A prow-tipped apex is boat-shaped, which is scaphoid. The bearer constraint is already limited to leaf parts.
The word means shortly sheathing. Mapping it to sheathing loses 'short', the extent of the sheath.
Cross-rugulose means finely wrinkled in a transverse direction. Plain rugose loses both the fineness and the direction.
Sappy means juicy or fleshy, so succulent fits for stems and herbs. The constraint is acceptable.
Dot-shaped means punctiform.
Stipe-like means resembling a stalk, so stipitate fits. The constraint covers parts that carry a stipe-like base.
'Relief' is a noun. It describes a surface pattern or the bearer's relief, not a quality that means 'raised'. Reject it, or handle it in a phrase rule.
Bulbose on a whole plant means it has a bulb. The constraint excludes bulbous hairs and other bulbous parts.
A flat-headed (flat-topped) inflorescence is corymb-like.
The phrase says the leaf bases do not persist, not that there is no leaf base. Mapping it to 'leaf base absent' is false, because a leaf base is present while the leaf is attached.
Infundibuliforme is the Latin/French form of funnel-shaped.
'Indistinctly delimited' is about boundaries that are unclear, not about conspicuousness.
Puberulent-glandular means minutely hairy with glands, which is a fine glandular pubescence. The loss of fineness is minor.
Half inferior describes an ovary and means the same as semi-inferior.
Short-exserted means only slightly protruding. Mapping it to exserted loses 'short'.
Trichome-bearing means hairy.
Squamate means scaly.
Not rooting at the nodes means there are no shoot-borne (adventitious) roots at the nodes. The bearer should be the stem.
Crinite means covered with long soft hairs, as in long-hairy. Bearded means hairs in a tuft or zone. This is a different quality. Use a long-hairy term instead.
A white powdery covering is mealy or farinose.
In descriptions, relieved (as in veins relieved) means standing out, which is prominent.
'Bunch' is a noun. It can mean a fruit bunch or a bunch of flowers, and is not the same as caespitose growth.
Vine-like means climbing or twining.
Phyllodial means having phyllodes, so a phyllode leaf is present.
Wire-like means thin and thread-like, which is filiform.
Ribbon-like means long, narrow and flat, which is strap-shaped.
Scabrid-denticulate means rough and finely toothed. Scabrous loses the toothed margin.
Cross-striolate means finely striated across the surface, which is transversely striated.
Stegocarpous mosses have a capsule opened by an operculum (lid). The bearer is the spore capsule.
Non-anastomosed means not anastomosing.
Deltate means triangular, so lance-deltate is lanceolate-triangular.
Chevron-shaped means V-shaped.
Arc-shaped means curved, as in arcuate.
'Rostered' appears to be a variant or misspelling of rostrate, which means beaked.
Sclerous means hardened, as with sclerenchyma.
Effaced means faded or obscure, which is inconspicuous.
Rim-like describes a margin or rim, not a ring. Ring shaped is the wrong shape.
Forming hummocks means growing as mounds or cushions. That is not the same as tufted caespitose growth.
Fistulose means hollow, so not fistulose means not hollow.
Faintly visible means barely seen, which is inconspicuous.
A bearer that does not reach the apex is not percurrent.
Non-ruminate means not ruminate.
Liana-like means climbing.
Not clasping means not clasping.
Not glaucous means not glaucous.
Compound-umbellate means the inflorescence is a compound umbel.
Rubiginous means rust-coloured, which is reddish brown.
'Tolerant to' is a relational quality that needs a stimulus. Mapping it loses 'drought'. Use a drought-specific term or a pattern with the stimulus.
Reticulate-venose means the venation forms a net, which is reticulate.
Dark-mottled is mottled. The dark colour is lost, but the pattern is kept.
A goblet shape is a cup shape on a stem, and cup-shaped is the nearest PATO term.
An umbel-like arrangement of cymes. umbelliform is defined for inflorescences only, and the 'cymose' part is lost.
Half-round matches semicircular.
'Subshrub-like' means suffrutescent, a woody base with herbaceous shoots. I could not find FLOPO_0987003 in the value-term file, so I did not check its definition.
'ecristate' means without a crest, so not crested is right.
Slightly sickle-shaped. falciform is the nearest term, and only the 'sub-' degree is lost.
'poreless' means without pores, so not porous.
The negation of dimorphic is stated directly.
'coniferous' means a conifer or cone-bearing taxon, or a forest type. It does not state that a particular bearer has a strobilus, so it is not a plain presence of a strobilus.
'rhombate' means rhombic, which is rhomboid.
'nonrhizomatous' means no rhizome.
'Continuous in color' means the colour is unbroken, for example in stripes or bands. concolorous means two compared surfaces have the same colour, which is a different meaning.
'humped' means swollen on one side, which fits the gibbous definition.
The shape is obovate. Only the width proportion ('broad') is lost, and that is a ratio, not a shape.
'Pectinately divided' means divided like a comb, which is pectinate.
prolate means an elongated ellipsoid. A broad ellipsoid is not elongated, so elliptic is the closer term.
'Lobulate' means with small lobes, and the pinnate arrangement is kept. This is close enough to pinnately lobed.
The word and the PATO term 'irregular thickness' mean the same thing.
'uncinulate' means finely hooked. uncinate is a synonym of falciform in the PATO lexicon.
'scaling' is exfoliating only for bark and other surfaces that peel. For other parts it can mean bearing scales.
The negation of coiled is stated directly.
'unfolded' means not folded. A leaf that has opened out is also not folded.
The brown colour is lost. 'Brown-dotted' is both dotted and brown, so it needs a colour plus punctate.
The negation of rosulate is stated directly.
'ecalyculate' means without a calyculus, and calyculus is a synonym of epicalyx.
'Semi-clasping' is partly clasping, and clasping is the nearest term. The degree is lost.
'lunar' means moon-shaped, which is crescent-shaped.
A plant that is not fragrant can still have another smell, so it is not odorless. A negated fragrant value would be right, but odorless is not.
'pollenless' means without pollen.
'quadripinnatifid' means four times pinnately cut, and tripinnate means three times. No four-times class exists.
In plant descriptions 'supine' means lying flat on the ground, which is prostrate.
'Without flecks' means not spotted.
'Pseudoaxillary' means apparently axillary but arising outside the true axil. extra-axillary is acceptable, but the 'appears axillary' part is lost.
Interwoven stems or hairs are tangled.
A tussock habit is a dense tuft growing from the base, which matches the caespitose definition.
A calicle is an epicalyx, so 'calicle-less' means no epicalyx.
'Pseudo-' means only apparently fascicled, so it should not be treated as truly fascicled.
'anastomous' is a variant spelling of anastomosing.
The negation of stipitate is stated directly.
'venulose' means with many fine veinlets. It describes the density and fineness of venation, not just that a vascular bundle is present.
Broadest at the middle fits elliptic and also oblong and other shapes. It describes where the widest point lies, not a shape.
The negation of petaloid is stated directly.
Semicamptodromous venation is a kind of pinnate venation. This maps to the parent term and loses the subtype. A camptodromous class, FLOPO_0991368, exists but is not an exact match.
Pleated is a synonym of plicate, so 'without pleats' means not plicate.
'farinose' means mealy, so not farinose is not mealy.
'scrotiform' means pouch-shaped, which fits the saccate definition.
Bladder-like structures are inflated.
'Distantly spaced' means widely separated, which is distant.
'ampullaceous' means flask-like, swollen with a narrow neck.
'inaequilateral' (inequilateral) means the two sides are unequal, which is asymmetrical.
Obtusely serrate teeth are still serrate. The degree word is lost, but the quality holds.
Virescent means becoming green or greenish, and green is the closest PATO term.
Curling backward is recurved.
Pellicular means thin and skin-like, which is membranous. I did not find the label of FLOPO_0991046 in the value-term file, so this rests on the rule's stated label.
Radicating means rooting, usually at nodes. That is shoot-borne roots present, and PO_0000042 lists adventitious root as a synonym.
French cannelée means channelled, fluted or grooved, which is furrowed.
Nervured means veined, and PO_0005020 lists vein as a synonym.
Non-peltate is the negation of peltate. FLOPO_0991107 is peltate under attachment quality.
Piano-convex is a spelling variant of plano-convex.
Hirtous means shaggy with stiff hairs, which is hirsute. The label of FLOPO_0991050 was not checked in the file.
Pungent-apiculate means a short tip that is also stiff and sharp. Mucronate is an abrupt small point and loses the pungency. A spine-tipped or apiculate mapping would also be partial.
A fringe of hairs is a fringed margin, as in ciliate.
Without a significant palea means the palea is absent or vestigial. The rule treats it as absent. The word 'significant' makes this a mild stretch.
Brick-shaped is rectangular.
Pungent can mean sharp-pointed or acrid in taste and smell. 'Not sharp' is right only for pointed parts, not for odour or taste.
Collapsing is collapsed. The wording is a process, but descriptions use it as a state.
Broadly ellipsoidal is elliptic. The degree of breadth is lost, but the shape holds.
Doubly serrulate (biserrulate) means small teeth that carry still smaller teeth. Plain serrulate loses the double toothing.
Tattering means the margin is irregularly torn, which is lacerate.
Incised-serrate means cut and toothed. Serrated keeps the teeth but loses the incision.
Without vittae means no oil tubes, as in Apiaceae fruits, so vitta absent. The FLOPO_0986042 id was not looked up.
Piriform means pear-shaped.
Hypocrateriform is the same as salverform. The word in the rule is a misspelling.
French incliné means inclined or slanting, which is an oblique orientation. It could also mean ascending or leaning.
French saillante means projecting, which is prominent.
Sarcotestal means the seed has a fleshy seed coat. 'Fleshy' belongs on the testa or seed coat only.
Tufted-pilose means hairs gathered in tufts, which is close to bearded (long hairs confined to a tuft). The pilose part is lost.
The prominence belongs to the nerves, not to the part. Prominent on the leaf would be wrong. The right form is vein with prominent, or a prominent-veined value.
Spinetipped is spine-tipped, written as one word.
Glandular-puncticulate means finely dotted with glands, which is gland-dotted.
Insipid means tasteless.
Pappose means having a pappus.
Ill-scented is foetid, which is an unpleasant odour.
Lamelliform means shaped like a plate or lamella.
Glandular-hairless is ambiguous. It may mean glandular and without hairs, or without glandular hairs. Rejected rather than mapped to glandular trichome absent.
Reticulate veined is reticulate venation.
Aristiform means awn- or bristle-like, which is close to setaceous.
Beak-shaped is close to beaked. It means shaped like a beak, while beaked means having a beak.
Comblike is pectinate.
Mallet-shaped means a head that is abruptly thicker than its stalk, which is close to clavate.
Without crest is not crested.
Ecalcarate means without a spur. The target is the corolla spur, so it is wrong for a spur on the calyx or sepals.
Incanous means hoary, with grey-white hairs, which is canescent.
Spathate means having a spathe, and PO_0009054 lists spathe as a synonym.
Not bearded is the negation of bearded.
Short-caulescent means a short stem. 'Stem present' loses the shortness, which is the point of the word.
Squamiform means scale-shaped.
Densely inserted means crowded.
Gymnostomous mosses have a capsule without a peristome.
Weakly thickened is thickened. The degree word is lost, but the quality holds.
Tetragonal means four-angled, which is what quadrangular means.
Buttress-free means not buttressed.
'Irregularly cut' also covers incised, laciniate or toothed margins. Lacerate means torn-looking. Better to reject or reduce to an edge-shape quality.
Non-corky is the plain negation of corky.
Poorly marked means faint or hard to see, which is inconspicuous.
Semi-superior is the same as half-inferior for an ovary.
Slit-shaped is the same as slit-like.
Bicucullate means two-hooded. Cucullate means one hood, so the count is lost.
Salveriform is a variant spelling of salverform.
Direct negation of heterostylous.
S-bent means S-shaped, which is sigmoid. PATO lists S-shaped as a synonym.
Pseudo-racemose means looking like a raceme, which is raceme-like.
Awl-like matches the PATO synonym awl-shaped for subulate.
Engraved means impressed or sunken into the surface. It is mostly used for veins and lines.
Narrowly paniculate is a panicle-like form. The 'narrowly' is a minor loss.
Non-crisped is the plain negation of crisped.
Not jointed is the plain negation of jointed.
Petioluliform means shaped like a small petiole. Clawed means abruptly narrowed at the base into a stalk, which is a different meaning.
Suffused with red means tinged or flushed with red. It does not mean the part is red.
Ovate is a flat 2-D outline broadest towards the base. It does not fit 3-D parts.
Indented does not mean the same as emarginate. Emarginate means notched at the apex. Indented covers any notching.
Vespertine means evening-active or evening-opening. Nocturnal means active at night, so the evening timing is lost.
Obovoid is a 3-D shape. For flat parts, broadest near the summit is obovate.
Lyrately pinnatifid is the lyrate leaf form.
Multicostate means having many ribs, which is ribbed.
Narrowly paniculiform is panicle-like. The 'narrowly' is a minor loss.
Pachycaul means thick-stemmed, so it only applies to stems.
Scalelike is a spelling variant of scale-like.
Angled upward means ascending.
Hardly narrowed means not tapered.
Not discernible means cannot be seen at all, which is closer to absent. Inconspicuous means present but hard to notice.
Plain negation of retuse.
Outcurving means curving outward. Recurved means curved backward or downward, so the direction differs.
Spicate-paniculate is a mixed form. Spike-like drops the panicle part.
Spicately arranged means arranged like a spike.
'Uniting' is generic (it can mean fusing). It means anastomosing only for veins.
Utriculiform means shaped like a small bladder or pouch, which is saccate.
The rule loses 'basal'. It would claim the gland is absent everywhere, when it is only absent at the base.
Corymbose-branched means branched like a corymb.
Without aril means aril absent.
Without paraphyses means paraphysis absent.
Plain negation of elongate.
Long-ellipsoid means a long, narrow ellipsoid. Elliptic loses the elongation.
Plain negation of sinuate.
Stylose means having a style.
Equal-sided means the two sides are equal, which is symmetrical.
Plain negation of plicate.
Unevenly thickened means irregular thickness.
The rule loses 'to exostome'. The attachment partner is part of the meaning, and a general 'adherent' misses it.
Plain negation of cucullate.
Eacarunculate means without a caruncle, so caruncle absent is right.
Scarcely abundant means few or rare, which fits decreased amount.
Cannelé is French for fluted or grooved, which is furrowed.
Densiflorous means densely flowered, which is a dense arrangement or number of flowers. Condensed loses the flowers.
Ecaliculate means without an epicalyx.
Evase (évasé) means flared, widening outward.
Narrow-sinused means the sinuses are narrow, not the whole part. Decreased width would land on the wrong bearer. The rule needs a sinus bearer.
Pubescent-velvety means hairy with velvety hairs, which is velutinous.
Without claw is not clawed, and FLOPO_0991169 is clawed.
French sarmenteux means with long, flexible, climbing stems, which is climbing.
Acumen is the acuminate tip, so without acumen is not acuminate.
Composite is ambiguous. It can mean compound, as in a compound leaf, or Asteraceae-type. It does not reliably mean a capitulum is present, and the rule would attach one to any part.
Splashed means irregularly blotched, which is mottled.
Thin-valved means the valves are thin. The rule drops the valve and would apply decreased thickness to the whole fruit.
Several-seriate means in several rows, which is multiseriate.
Frilly means ruffled or finely wavy, which is crisped.
Not aculeate means without prickles, so not spiny.
A semisuperior ovary is the same as a half-inferior one.
A bristle-terminated part ends in a bristle or seta. That is not the same as having an awn, and the rule leaves out which part carries it.
Decorated means ornamented.
Glandular dots matches the definition of gland-dotted.
Midnerved means having a midrib. Leaf midvein is only right for leaves. Sepals, bracts and other parts need their own midvein.
Not root-sprouting means no suckers arise from the roots, which is root-borne shoot system absent.
Retrorsely barbed means barbs pointing backward, which matches the definition of barbed.
Spirally ranked means arranged in a spiral.
Tailless means without a tail, so not caudate.
Thyrses describes a thyrse-type inflorescence, which is thyrse-like. The plural form could also be read as an entity, so confidence is modest.
Wide-ovate means broadly ovate, which is a kind of ovate. The width is lost, but ovate is a valid parent class.
Without abaxial keel means the keel on the lower surface is missing. Not keel-shaped drops the abaxial keel as the bearer. Keel (carina) absent would be better.
Without tubers is tuber absent.
Dichasiate means arranged in dichasia, and a dichasium is a cyme. PO lists dichasium as a synonym.
Flower-bearing means it carries flowers, so flower present.
Armed means bearing spines, prickles or thorns, so not armed is not spiny.
Ladderlike is scalariform, so the negation is right.
Prolate means elongated. Short-ellipsoid means a short ellipsoid, nearly rounded, so it is not prolate. An ellipsoid class would fit better.
Abruptly expanded is dilated. The abruptness is lost, but the main meaning stays.
Granular-puberulent means finely hairy and also granular. Puberulous loses the granular texture.
Helmet-like means hooded, which is cucullate.
Rod-like is a listed synonym of cylindrical.
Saccate-dilated means pouch-like swollen, which is saccate.
Shrublike means shrubby in habit, which matches frutescent habit.
Without ridges is not ridged.
Brilliant means shining, which is glistening. It can also describe a bright colour, so confidence is modest.
Conjoined means joined together, which is connate.
Glandular-spotted means marked with gland dots.
Not setose is the negation of setose.
Not spongy is the negation of spongy.
A pipe-like calyx is a tube, which is tubular, and the rule is already limited to the calyx.
Puce is a dark purplish brown-red, close to dark purplish red.
Sanguineous means blood-red, which is deep red.
Slipper-shaped (calceolate) is a specific pouch shape, as in a lip or labellum. Saccate is a general pouch or bag.
Drops 'sparsely'. The density of the hairs is lost, and sparsely hirsute is not the same as hirsute.
'Unclear' means indistinct. That fits inconspicuous only for features such as veins or markings.
Without caruncle means the caruncle is absent.
The rule is already restricted to corolla. Without spurs means the corolla spur is absent.
Crest-like is cristate, which is crested.
Fine-meshed means a net-like pattern with small meshes. The mesh size is a minor loss.
Drops 'pale'. This is a lighter shade of chestnut brown, not chestnut.
Lobate is a variant spelling of lobed, so pinnately lobate means pinnately lobed.
Setulose means with small bristles, which is not the same as pubescent. The target loses the setulose part. Glandular-pubescent is a different hair type.
Mealy keeps the powdery texture but drops the white colour. White and powdery are two qualities.
Equally long is equal in length. Equal is equal in size, which is broader.
Mid-veined means having a midvein.
Nerveless usually means no visible veins in a leaf-like part. A vascular bundle is a different, internal structure. It is correct only if the leaf vein is meant.
Olive-shaped is a 3-D ovoid or ellipsoid form, not the 2-D elliptic outline. I found no good target.
Oval is a common botanical word for broadly elliptic.
Biarticulated means two-jointed. The number of joints is lost.
Pentahedral means five-faced and is 3-D. Pentagonal is a 2-D five-sided outline.
Bi- means twice pinnatisect. The double division is lost.
Drops 'short'. Short-rhombic is a proportion of the rhomboid shape.
Drops 'broadly', the degree of leaf-likeness.
The prefix e- means without, so esinuose means without sinuses, i.e. not sinuous.
Lax walled means loose or flaccid walls, not thin walls. No thickness is stated.
Nondecurrent means not decurrent.
'Not separating' is ambiguous. It can mean not splitting or not dehiscing, or not falling off. It does not clearly mean non-deciduous.
Rhizoidiferous means bearing rhizoids.
The strength belongs to the stem. Robust on the plant loses the bearer.
The quality is about the lateral walls, not the whole part. The bearer is lost.
Arcuate is one kind of curve, so not arcuate does not mean not curved. The part may still be curved in another way.
Not spurred is stated for different parts. The rule is correct only when the part is the corolla or a petal. A calyx or sepal spur is a different structure.
Piliform means hair-like, which is finer than the thread-like filiform.
Tuberized means swollen like a tuber, which is tuberous.
Bracteoliform means shaped like a bracteole, a small bract. Bract-like is close enough.
Fused to the apex of another part is adnation, not connation. Connate means fused with like parts, and the attachment point is lost.
Non-articulated means not jointed.
Repliable means able to be folded back. It is not the same as folded.
Curvilinear means following curved lines, which is curved.
Domatia-bearing means domatia are present.
Fauve means tawny, a yellowish brown.
Translucent dots are often glands but are not always so. The gland meaning is added.
