Homomorphous means all of one form. Not dimorphic also allows three or more forms.
Lenticel-free means no lenticels.
Unguiculate means clawed, so not unguiculate means not clawed.
Asperulate means slightly rough, which is close to scabrous.
Intraxylary phloem is a synonym of internal phloem in the PO lexicon.
Scarcely apparent means barely visible, which is inconspicuous.
Subconic means almost conical, a normal approximation.
Non-overlapping means not imbricate.
Twin means two together, which is paired.
Veinlet is a synonym of higher order leaf vein, so without included veinlets means these are absent.
Non-tubular means not tubular.
Hyacinth-scented names a specific scent. Mapping it to sweet-scented loses that.
Not flaking means not exfoliating, usually said of bark.
Stomata-free means the stomata are absent.
A falsely racemose inflorescence only resembles a raceme, so raceme-like fits.
Seedy means containing seeds. It is read as seed present, and only in fruit contexts.
Bunchy means clustered. It matches caespitose (tufted) only for the habit of the whole plant or its shoots.
Not peeling means not exfoliating, usually said of bark.
Waited is almost certainly an OCR or typing error for waisted, and no other sense is plausible in a flora. A rule that fixes it is acceptable.
Whippy means flexible and slender, so flexible is a fair target.
A lacerate-margined part has a lacerate margin.
Coalescing parts are fused, which is the sense of connate.
Straplike means strap-shaped.
Mushy means soft, usually of fruit or tissue.
Articulating means having a joint, which is jointed.
Auricle-less means without auricles, so not auriculate.
Bland is a taste word. It applies only to parts that are tasted.
Cymulose means bearing cymules, a form of cyme. The PO cyme class lists cymule as a synonym.
Glassy usually means shiny or lustrous, or transparent. It does not reliably mean translucent, so the rule should be rejected.
Hirtello-puberulent combines short stiff hairs (hirtellous) with puberulent. Puberulous alone loses the stiff-hair part.
Incoherent means not coherent, as in not fused or not cohering.
The adverb narrowly is only a degree. The shape is clavate.
Not appressed is the negation of appressed.
Not leaflike is the negation of leaf-like.
Not oblique is the negation of oblique.
Not reflexing is read as not reflexed.
Not ridged is the negation of ridged.
Spinulose-aristate means minutely spiny and awned. Spine-tipped loses the awn (aristate) part.
Uncompressed means not flattened.
Widely ovate is ovate. The adverb only gives the degree.
A base gradually narrowed is tapered. The base is the part, and tapered is the quality.
Blade-bearing means having a lamina.
Broadly expanded means dilated.
Bulblet-bearing means having bulblets. The PO bulb class lists bulblet as a synonym.
Chalk white is white.
Clavulate is a diminutive of clavate, so it is clavate.
Coarsely reticulate is reticulate. The adverb only gives the degree.
Featherlike is plumose, and PATO lists feathery as a synonym.
Not cleft is the negation of cleft.
Not slender is the negation of slender.
Spinose means spiny, so not spinose is not spiny.
Remotely spaced means distant.
Shallowly saucer-shaped is saucer-shaped. The adverb only gives the degree.
Smudged means marked with smears or blotches, so blotchy is close enough.
Sparsely scattered means sparse.
Thyrselike means thyrse-like.
Bifarious means arranged in two rows, which is distichous.
Bulky means large in volume. Increased size is acceptable.
Callose-apiculate means a short point with a callose (hard, thickened) tip. Mucronate loses the callose part.
Carpellate means bearing carpels but no stamens, which is female. The bearer constraint is appropriate.
Caudate-cuspidate is an intermediate apex (tail-like and abruptly pointed). Caudate alone drops the cuspidate half.
A compound corymbose inflorescence is still corymb-like; 'compound' only describes the branching.
A cymose panicle has cymose branching. 'Panicle-like' drops that, and the target is defined as a panicle with stalked flowers on the branches.
'Fat' means thick for these organs. Elsewhere it is ambiguous, for example 'fat' seeds or fruit may mean plump or wide.
'Hardly expanded' means only slightly expanded. 'Not dilated' turns a matter of degree into a flat negation.
Lacerate is defined as an irregularly cut margin, so the adverb is redundant.
Lianoid means liana-like and climbing.
Lignose is a variant of ligneous (woody).
The target ovate is a 2-D outline and loses 'long' (elongate). Long-ovoid is closer to oblong-ovate.
Non-climbing is the plain negation of climbing.
Non-tuberous is the plain negation of tuberous.
Barbate is a synonym of bearded, so the negation holds.
Corniculate means with small horns, which fits horned, so the negation holds.
Not lignified means not woody, which is not ligneous.
The radiate target is defined for capitula (heads), and the bearer constraint already limits the rule to them.
Obcolumnar is not an obconical shape. Obconical is an inverted cone, and obcolumnar is not a standard term.
Polyphyllous means made of free separate leaves or segments. That is right for a whorl such as a perianth or involucre, not for other parts.

Not acuminate is the negation of acuminate.
Not acuminated is the negation of acuminate.
Not bifid is the negation of bifid. PATO has bifid as a synonym of bifurcated.
Not buttressed is the negation of buttressed.
Not muricate is the negation of muricate.
Obtus-arrondi means obtuse and rounded. Obtuse alone loses the rounded part.
Plan is the French for flat or level.
Poorly apparent means inconspicuous.
Pseudo-paniculate means panicle-like.
Rachisless means the rachis is absent.
Rayonnant is the French for radiating.
Semi-orbiculate means half-round, which is semicircular.
Unfissured means not fissured.
Unique, as a translation of the French, means a single one, which is solitary.

target: connate + basally (the base as the bearer or a position)
reason: The words at base are lost. The parts are united only at the base and may be free above.
A visible vein is a conspicuous vein, and the rule is limited to veins.
Wheel-like is the usual gloss of rotate, as in a rotate corolla.
Évasé is the French for flared.
Bad-smelling means foetid.
Dangling means pendent.
Bloom is the waxy coating, so lacking bloom means not glaucous.
Lacking endosperm means the endosperm is absent.
Spike-shaped means spike-like.
Circumferential means running around the circumference, as in circumscissile dehiscence. That is not the same as surrounding another structure.
Flattenuated looks like a blend of flattened and attenuated. Mapping it to flattened alone loses the attenuate part.
A jasmine scent is a sweet scent. The rule loses the type of scent but is accurate.
Non-verticillate means not whorled, so the negated whorled target fits.
Not angular is the negation of angular.
Not marginal is the negation of the marginal position value. I could not read the FLOPO_0991208 definition, so this is less certain.
Not truncate is the negation of truncated.
Smelly only says that a smell is present. It is not necessarily foul, and FLOPO_0991020 is defined as an unpleasant, offensive odour. A plain odour quality is safer.
Basi-dorsifixed means attached by the back at the base. Plain dorsifixed loses the basal position.
Flabellate venation is fan-like. Actinodromous means several primary veins radiating from one point. The two are not the same, so the rule should be rejected.
Ventricose means swollen or bellied, usually in the middle. Gibbous means swollen on one side. Negating a loose synonym is unreliable.
This is a misspelling of anastomosing.
The FLOPO ovate definition is broadest below the middle, towards the base. The match is loose, since the egg-shaped outline is implied rather than stated.
Cobweb-like is the meaning of arachnose.
Filmy means very thin and translucent, which is membranous.
Flesh-coloured means pale pink.
This is a typo for inconspicuous.
Non-beaked is the negation of beaked.
Pinnately nerved is pinnately veined. Nerve and vein are used for the same thing.
Stinking is foetid.
Streaky is streaked.
A tetrahedron is a triangular pyramid, so subtetrahedral is close to pyramidal. The match is approximate.
Wide-angled branching or spreading is divaricate. The match is approximate.
Widest in the middle, with both ends narrowing, is elliptic.
Darker lines on a surface is the streaked pattern.
Tolerant to is relational and needs a stressor. The rule loses that it is drought that is tolerated.
A frayed margin is irregularly torn, which is lacerate.
Leaf-shaped is leaf-like.
Nodeless means the stem has no nodes, so stem node absent is right.
Pulpy means soft and juicy. A part can be fleshy without being pulpy, so not pulpy does not mean not fleshy.
Right-twining names the twining direction (clockwise), and plain climbing loses it. Twining is only one kind of climbing.
String-like is thread-like, which is filiform.
Comose means a terminal tuft of hairs on a seed or fruit. A tuft of hairs on other parts, such as leaf axils or nodes, is not comose.
Biglobular means made of two globose parts. Bilobed means having two lobes.
Connate-perfoliate means the leaf bases are fused and surround the stem. Plain connate loses the perfoliate meaning.
Densely distributed means crowded.
Dust-like means powdery or very fine. It does not mean a decrease in size, because decreased size is relative.
Fringeless means not fringed.
Non-peeling means not exfoliating. Peeling is a listed synonym of exfoliating.
Acuneate is not a standard term, and the rule reads it as cuneate. If it is a negation, it would be not cuneate, and the sense is unclear.
Strigillose is strigulose, which has small, appressed, stiff hairs. Adpressed adds nothing, because strigose hairs are already appressed.
Bark-covered means bark is present.
Brownish buff is a pale tan-brown, close to light brown.
Campaniform is bell-shaped, which is campanulate.
Cinerous means ash-grey.
Cork-like is corky.
Cymose-fasciculate describes a cyme-like arrangement of fascicles. Plain fascicled loses the cymose structure.
A depressed ellipsoid is flattened at the poles, which is an oblate spheroid. The match is approximate.
This is a typo for ellipsoid, and PATO lists ellipsoid as a synonym of elliptic.
Fulcate is a typo for falcate.
Gibberulous is a diminutive of gibbous, meaning slightly swollen on one side.
Half-sheathing means the base partly clasps the stem, like half-amplexicaul. The match is approximate.
Ill-odoured is foul-smelling.
'inbricate' is a spelling error for imbricate (overlapping).
Lenticelled means bearing lenticels, so 'lenticel present' fits.
Liver-coloured means dark reddish brown.
Channelled means grooved, so 'not channelled' is 'not grooved'.
A direct negation of mottled.
A direct negation of opaque.
A direct negation of petiolate. The bearer constraint is already in the registry.
'Not rebranching' says the branches are not branched again. 'Unbranched' on a plant or stem would say there are no branches at all, which is different.
Partially joined parts are connate. The degree of fusion is lost, which is acceptable.
Peach scent is a pleasant fruity smell and no more specific class exists. Only the kind of scent is lost.
Saw-like margins are serrate.
Semi-lunate means half-moon or crescent shaped.
Sloughing bark or skin is shedding or exfoliating.
Bark peeling in strips is exfoliating.
Only the hyphenation differs from subacute.
Thorned means bearing thorns.
Tripinnately compound is the definition of tripinnate.
Umbellulate means bearing umbellules, or arranged in small umbels. It is an inflorescence term and is not umbel-shaped for other parts.
Wedge-like is cuneate, and the lexicon lists wedge-shaped as a synonym.
The rule loses 'apical'. It would say that all secretory tissue or glands are absent, when the text says only the apical glands are absent.
Papillae are epidermal papilla cells, so 'papilla cell absent' fits.
Stipel is the right class and absence is expressed correctly.
The phrase gives only where the widest point is. Elliptic also requires both ends to taper alike, and an oblong blade is also widest at the middle.
Crispulate means slightly crisped, which is the same character.
'Inverted' is lost. An inverted Y is a different shape from a Y.
A long oval outline is elliptic or oblong-elliptic. This is a loose match.
Racemed means arranged in racemes, which is the same as raceme-like.
A racemose-cymose inflorescence is a thyrse, with a racemose axis and cymose branches.
Slender cylindric is cylindrical. Only the degree is lost.
Strophiole absent is the correct absence pattern.
Lacking spines is the same as not spiny.
Ocellate means marked with eye-like spots. Spotted is the closest class, and the ring detail is lost.
Fasciculiform means in the form of a fascicle, so fascicled fits.
Semi-translucent is translucent to a degree.
Annulus-shaped is ring shaped.
The lexicon lists hooked and uncinate as synonyms of falciform.
For leaves 'divided' means cut or dissected into segments, not branched. A branching class would give the wrong meaning. A dissected-type class could be better, but I did not look one up.
With palea means a palea is present. I did not confirm the PO label.
Nodal root is a synonym of shoot-borne nodal root.
Smooth-edged means an entire margin.
Umbrella-like inflorescences are umbel-shaped, and the constraint is already set.
Plinerved means the main veins diverge from above the base. This can be acrodromous or actinodromous, so the target adds a claim.
Glandular granules are gland dots. The match is close.
Polliniferous means bearing pollen.
Proliferous bulbils are bulbils, and the absence pattern fits.
Submembranaceous means somewhat membranous.
'Tinged' means only slightly coloured, so the part is not red brown overall.
Subarcuate means somewhat arched, which is curved.
Dependent means hanging down, which is pendent.
'Brownish-tinged' means only a slight brown tinge, not brown overall.
Sublustrous means somewhat lustrous, which is glossy or shiny.
Pelviform means basin-shaped, which is bowl shaped.
Lacking colleters means the colleter is absent.
Tinged means only partly or faintly coloured. Mapping it to purplish red for the whole part loses that.
Subimpressed means slightly sunken, as in impressed veins. PATO sunken fits.
Glandular-resinous means glandular and resinous. Mapping to resinous alone loses the glandular part.
Resin-gland-dotted means dotted with resin glands. Gland-dotted keeps the meaning.
Thinnish means rather thin, which is decreased thickness.
Boatlike means boat-shaped, which is scaphoid (navicular).
Lateral bracts are only some of the bracts. Without lateral bracts does not mean the bract is absent.
Cross-reticulate is a reticulate pattern with cross veins.
Subumbellate describes inflorescence architecture, and the umbelliform term is constrained to inflorescences.
Scabrellate means slightly scabrous.
Subcompressed means slightly flattened.
Mound-forming describes a plant's growth form, which is cushion-like. It does not apply to ordinary organs, where pulvinate means a swollen, cushion-like organ.
Foldless means not folded.
Multiheaded means having several heads (capitula). That is a count of heads, not branching. Use a counted-part rule for heads.
Not withered means not shrivelled, so the part is fresh. The match is close but not exact.
Cicatrose means scarred or scar-marked, which is cicatricial.
Tinged means only faintly yellow. Mapping it to plain yellow loses that.
Subexserted means slightly exserted.
Short-silky is sericeous with short hairs. Mapping to sericeous alone loses the short length of the hairs.
Noncircinate means not circinate.
Several-rayed means having several rays, as in umbel rays or ray florets. That is a count. It is not a star shape.
Semirotund means half-round, which is semicircular.
Un-twisted means not twisted.
Scar-covered means scarred.
Without fibres means not fibrous.
Paniculate-branched means branched like a panicle.
Oviform means egg-shaped. PATO ovate is for flat outlines, and solid parts such as fruit and seed need the ovoid class.
Panicle-shaped means panicle-like.
Cellular-reticulate means a net-like pattern of cells, which is reticulate.
Flagged means bearing a flag, as in a flag petal or a flag leaf, or ribbon-like. It does not mean the leaf lamina is present.
Bulbiferous means bearing bulbils (aerial bulbs), and PO lists bulbil as a synonym of aerial tuber.
Unsegmented means not segmented.
The rule drops 'axillary'. Bulblets elsewhere on the plant are not excluded, and the PO bulb class is not specific to axillary bulblets.
Seasonally green means green only in the growing season, so it is not simply deciduous. It is a loss of leaf colour and not necessarily of leaves.
Without gibbosity means not gibbous.
Equally sized means equal in size across a set of parts.
Close-fitting means lying closely against another structure, which is appressed.
Fruticulose means somewhat shrubby, which is a habit of the whole plant. It is not frutescent in the strict sense.
Squamose means scaly.
Tomentellate means finely or slightly tomentose.
The absence is only of a central bundle of paraphyses. Paraphyses may still be present elsewhere, so paraphysis absent is too strong.
Infundibulate means funnel-shaped.
Closely flowered means flowers close together, which is a condensed inflorescence.
Cross-zoned means crossed by bands, which is banded.
Not beadlike means not moniliform.
Multidichotomously means forking repeatedly. Bifurcated is a single fork.
Evenly coloured means one colour throughout, which is concolorous.
'Spaced apart' means distant spacing, as in leaves or teeth.
Glochidiform means shaped like a glochid, with barbed tips.
Nonadherent is the plain negation of adherent.
The phrase is a compound shade (light grayish straw-coloured brown). Mapping it to plain 'light brown' loses the grayish and straw tones.
Crispate means crisped, so 'not crispate' is the negation.
'Palmately' gives the pattern (palmate striations or veins). Plain 'striated' loses it.
Silklike hairs are silky, which is the PATO synonym of sericeous.
'Stellately' says the scales are star-shaped. Plain 'scaly' loses that.
'Thinly' weakens leathery (subcoriaceous or chartaceous). Coriaceous means fully leathery.
'Without folds' is the negation of folded.
Erumpent means bursting through the surface, which is a kind of protruding.
Vestite means clothed with hairs or other covering. In floras it nearly always means hairy.
Cobwebby-woolly combines arachnoid and lanate. Plain 'lanate' drops the cobwebby (thin, loose) part.
Refracted means bent abruptly backward, which is reflexed.
'Lacking reticulation' is the negation of reticulate.
It is a direct negation of marcescent.
Cobwebby-felted combines arachnoid and felted. Plain 'pannose' drops the cobwebby part.
'Without pollen' means pollen is absent.
Brochidodrome is the noun form of brochidodromous (loop-forming secondary veins).
Exalate means without wings.
Atomiferous means bearing minute dots, so glandular-atomiferous is gland-dotted.
Non-glanduliferous means bearing no glands. PO has 'gland' as a synonym of secretory tissue.
A glomerule is a compact cluster-type inflorescence. The generic inflorescence class is safe.
It is the plural of glomerule.
It is the French form of glomerule.
In floras, pulp is nearly always fruit pulp or flesh.
'Pulpe' is the French form of fruit pulp.
'Fruit pulp' is the fruit flesh, a PO synonym.
Hair is a PO synonym of trichome.
Dichasium is a PO synonym of cyme inflorescence.
It is the plural of dichasium.
It is the French form of dichasium.
Only for branches of an inflorescence. Vegetative 'primary branch' (trees, shoots) is not an inflorescence axis.
Same as R2233: only correct inside an inflorescence. Vegetative primary branches are not meant.
Same as R2233 in French: only correct inside an inflorescence.
It is the French plural of dichasie.
Stilt roots are aerial adventitious roots, a PO synonym of shoot-borne root.
'Stilt root' is a PO synonym.
It is the plural of stilt root.
'Racine échasse' is the French for stilt root.
Involucre lobes are lobes of a fused involucre, not separate bracts. No PO class exists for them, so they are better left unmapped or given a new class.
Same as R2241: lobes of a fused involucre are not involucral bracts.
Same as R2241: lobes of a fused involucre are not involucral bracts.
A 'floral tube' is often the fused calyx or corolla tube, not a hypanthium. It is safe only where the text means the hypanthium, such as in Myrtaceae, Lythraceae and Rosaceae.
'Floral cup' is a PO synonym of hypanthium.
Cocci are the separating fruit segments, which are mericarps.
It is the singular of cocci.
A nectary scale is a scale-like floral nectary.
It is the plural of nectary scale.
'Nectar scale' is a variant of nectary scale.
Nectar scales are scale-like nectaries in the flower, so flower nectary fits.
French 'squamule nectarifère' means a nectar-bearing scale, which is a flower nectary.
Plural of R2252; same meaning.
Nectar-bearing scale, i.e. a nectary. Same meaning as R2252.
An anther appendage can be an extension of the connective, but it can also be a spur or awn on the thecae (e.g. Ericaceae). Mapping all of them to the connective is wrong. The anther is safer.
Plural of R2255; same problem.
An apical appendage is often a connective prolongation, but not always. The rule loses the generic meaning, and the anther is safer.
French equivalent of R2255; same problem.
'Perianth part' is generic. In a flower with calyx and corolla it means a sepal or petal, so tepal is too specific.
Plural of R2259; same problem.
'Perianth segment' usually means a tepal. A lobe of a fused perianth is a rare exception.
Plural of R2261.
French 'pièce du périanthe' is generic and covers sepals, petals and tepals.
Plural of R2263; same problem.
'Perianth member' is generic and can be a sepal or petal as well as a tepal.
French 'foliole' means leaflet.
Plural of 'foliole'.
Latin 'foliolum' means leaflet.
'Bloom' alone often means flowers or flowering, not wax. It also means a glaucous coating. It cannot be mapped to epicuticular wax without context.
A waxy bloom is the epicuticular wax coating.

Fascicles also occur in leaves (pine needles), stamens (Hypericum), hairs, roots and vascular bundles. Flower fascicle fits only fascicles of flowers or inflorescences, so it needs a constraint on the container.
Singular of R2271; same problem. 'Fascicle' alone does not mean a flower cluster.
French 'fascicule' is equally generic: it is used for leaf, stamen and flower bundles.
Plural of R2273; same problem.
Endostome segments are the inner peristome. Peristome tooth would merge them with exostome teeth and lose the inner/outer distinction.
Plural of R2275; same problem.
Same as R2275; the endostome identity is lost.
Same as R2275; 'inner' is lost.
In ferns and seed plants the sporophyte is the whole plant. In bryophytes it is only the dependent capsule and seta, so it is not a whole plant.
Plural of R2279; same problem.
A spatheole is a small spathe, i.e. an inflorescence bract.
Plural of R2281.
French 'spathéole' is a small spathe, an inflorescence bract.
Plural of R2283.
A collective vein is the vein running close to the lamina margin, which is the intramarginal vein.
Plural of R2285.
'Collecting vein' is a variant of collective vein, i.e. the intramarginal vein.
Plural of R2287.
French 'nervure collectrice' is the collective (intramarginal) vein.
A rachilla is the ultimate inflorescence axis, such as a palm branchlet or a spikelet axis. It is a higher-order inflorescence axis.
Singular of R2290.
Spelling variant of rachilla.
French plural of rachille.
The PO lexicon lists gametophyte as a synonym of whole plant. It is acceptable for bryophyte or fern gametophytes.
Plural of R2294.
A cross-vein is a small connecting vein between main veins. Leaf lamina vein loses the 'connecting' meaning. The word is also used for insect wings.
Plural of R2296; same problem.
Spelling variant of R2296; same problem.
On a plant a secondary axis is a branch. In an inflorescence it is a second-order axis, which is a higher order inflorescence axis (PO_0009081), not a branch.
Plural of R2299; same problem.
'Secondary axis' is a listed synonym of branch.
Plural of R2301.
Midrib is a listed synonym of leaf midvein.
French for the midrib.
French for the central vein, which is the midrib.
A pseudoraceme is an inflorescence. The raceme-like type is lost, but the bearer is right.
Spelling variant of R2306.
French form of R2306.
Plural of R2308.
A probract is a bract-like leaf at the base of an inflorescence or flower. Bract is the nearest class.
Plural of R2310.
'probractée' is an adjective meaning 'having probracts'. It is not a part, so it should not be a bearer.
Plural of the adjective in R2312. It describes a part and is not one.
A geniculum is a knee-like bend. It is a pulvinus-like joint only on a petiole. On culms, nodes and palm parts it is a different structure.
Plural of R2314, with the same limit.
A bent or swollen joint of the petiole is the petiole pulvinus.
A tubular sheath is a leaf sheath or a sheathing base. A scale leaf (cataphyll) is a different organ.
Plural of R2317.
A sterile sheath is a sheath around a sterile part, as in ferns or Cyperaceae. It is not a scale leaf. Use leaf sheath only when it is clearly a leaf sheath.
Border is a plain synonym of margin.
Plural of R2320.
'Inflorescence branch' is a listed synonym of higher order inflorescence axis.
Plural of R2322.
French for the branches of the panicle.
A pseudopetiole is a narrowed, stalk-like base of the blade. It is not a true petiole, so leaf lamina base fits.
Plural of R2325.
French form of R2325.
Acorn is a listed synonym of nut fruit.
Plural of R2328.
A primary bract is an inflorescence bract, as in the involucre of umbels. It is somewhat broad.
The primary nerve is the primary leaf vein or midvein. It is not a secondary vein.
A clump is a tufted plant. The lexicon already has 'woody clump' under whole plant.
The sarcotesta is only the fleshy outer layer of the testa. Mapping it to the whole testa gives the whole testa the layer's qualities, such as fleshy and colour.
Plural of R2333, with the same problem.
An umbellet is the secondary umbel of a compound umbel, which is a second order inflorescence.
French for umbellet.
Spelling variant of R2336.
A partial umbel is a ray umbel of a compound umbel.
The position between the stamens is lost, because it maps to a generic secretory tissue. A bearer rule can only use this class if a flower container is set.
French form of R2339, with the same problem.
A partial inflorescence is a branch unit of a compound inflorescence.
French form of R2341.
A false raceme is an inflorescence that looks like a raceme. The class is general but right.
French form of R2343.
The claw is the narrow stalk-like base of a petal.
Same meaning as R2345.
'Shoot' is a listed synonym of shoot system. 'Leafy' only describes it.
Vein is a synonym of vascular bundle, but 'longitudinal vein' in a leaf is a leaf vein. The class is right only for parts that have longitudinal veins.
French form of R2348, with the same limit.
Petiolar gland is a listed synonym of extrafloral nectary.
PO lists 'petiolar gland' as a synonym of extrafloral nectary. Petiolar glands in floras are normally nectar glands.
The plural of leaf.
A pseudo-staminode is a structure that looks like a staminode but is not a sterile stamen. Mapping it to staminode (PO_0009077) loses the 'not a stamen' meaning. It is better left unmapped.
Same as R2353: a pseudo-staminodium is not a true staminode.
A syncarp is a fruit formed from fused carpels, or a multiple fruit. Fruit is the right part.
In French, 'syncarpe' is often the adjective for a gynoecium or ovary with fused carpels ('ovaire syncarpe'), not the fruit. Match it only when it is a noun for the fruit.
The plural of syncarp, a fruit. An English adjective plural is unlikely.
PO gives 'vein' as a synonym of vascular bundle. The 'major' rank is lost but the part is right.
Corona segments are the parts of a corona (as in Asclepiadaceae and Passiflora), which fits corona lobe.
The plural of corona segment.
'vitae' is a variant spelling of 'vittae', the plural of vitta (oil tube in Apiaceae fruits).
Receptacular scales (paleae or chaff in Asteraceae) are a synonym of flower bract (chaff) in PO.
The plural of receptacular scale.
The French form of receptacular scale (palea).
A receptacle tube is the hypanthium, the floral cup (as in Myrtaceae and Rosaceae).
Same as R2365, with a space instead of a hyphen.
A strand is a portion of sclerenchyma tissue. PO lists 'portion of sclerenchyma tissue' as a synonym.
The plural of sclerenchyma strand.
Another phrasing of sclerenchyma strand.
The replum is the persistent partition of a fruit (as in Brassicaceae).
'repla' is the plural of replum.
PO's 'sporangium neck' synonym fits the apophysis of a moss capsule. In angiosperm fruits a 'capsule neck' is not a sporangium base.
Same as R2372.
Same as R2372.
PO gives 'cone scale' as a synonym of megasporophyll (ovuliferous scale). Scales of pollen cones are microsporophylls, so the rule is correct only for seed cones.
Same as R2375.
The leaf axis of a compound leaf or frond is the rachis.
The plural of leaf axis.
The French plural of leaf axis.
The French singular of leaf axis.
'Stamen tube' means the same as staminal tube.
The plural of stamen tube.
The French form of staminal tube.
The French form of staminal tube, with the feminine ending.
'arista' is a synonym of awn in PO. The plural 'aristae' is also an awn.
'aristés' is the French adjective 'awned', not the noun. It describes a feature (awn present) and is not a part to use as a bearer. It should be an entity-presence rule for awn.
Underleaves are the ventral leaves of liverworts, a kind of non-vascular leaf. The ventral position is lost, but no more specific class exists.
The plural of underleaf.
An offset is a short lateral shoot from the base of the plant. This is close to a basal axillary shoot (PO synonyms: tiller and ratoon).
The plural of offset.
Involucral leaves are the bracts of the involucre.
The plural of involucral leaf.
These are the involucral bracts of the primary umbel or head. The 'primary' rank is lost but the part is right.
'viscidia' is the Latin plural of viscidium.
The French singular of viscidium.
The French plural of viscidium.
A segment of a leaf blade is a division of the lamina, which fits leaf lamina lobe. In palms and compound leaves it may mean a leaflet.
Same as R2397.
'Stigmatic lobe' means the same as stigma lobe.
The plural of stigmatic lobe.
French 'lobe stigmatique' is the lobe of a stigma.
Plural of R2401.
Basal nerves are the veins that leave the base of a leaf blade (palmate or plinerved leaves).
Plural of R2403.
French plural of R2403; 'nervure' is a vein.

A hair-point is a slender, often hyaline tip on an apex. It is not the apex itself. It also occurs on bracts, glumes and sepals. The existing value term hair-pointed (FLOPO:0991249) already covers the meaning. Keep it as a word-to-quality rule or reject it.
Plural of R2406. The hair-like tip is lost, and the part may not be a leaf.
Same as R2406. A hair point is a tip, not the apex.
'Hyaline' is a quality and the hair-point is only a tip of the apex. Same problem as R2406.
Limb of a leaf is the blade; 'leaf blade' is a synonym of leaf lamina.
Same as R2410.
Plural of peristome tooth.
Primary rays of an umbel are the first branches of the main axis. PO lists 'primary inflorescence branch' as a synonym of second order inflorescence axis.
Plural of R2413.
French form of R2413.
A male spike is a staminate inflorescence. The spike shape is lost, but the class is right.
A staminate spike is a staminate inflorescence.

'Serration' mostly names the state of the margin (serrate, a quality), not the tooth. It is a tooth only in counts or sizes such as 'serrations 3 per cm'. A word-only rule would turn margin descriptions into tooth statements.
Same as R2418. 'Crenation' names the crenate state of the margin more often than a tooth.
'Stock' usually means a rootstock or caudex-like base. It can also be the grafting stock or the garden plant Matthiola. Calling it stem loses the meaning. It is better rejected.
PO lists 'male inflorescence' as a synonym of staminate inflorescence.
Plural of colleter.
Colleter is right, but the rule loses that the colleter is on the calyx. Add the calyx (PO_0009060) as container_id.
A pseudopedicel is a stalk-like part that is not a true pedicel, so the generic stalk is acceptable.
A bract on the peduncle of an inflorescence is an inflorescence bract.
A pseudopanicle is an inflorescence. The specific form has no PO class, so the generic class is the safe choice.
A cymose panicle is an inflorescence. The generic class is safe.
'Phyllaryphyll' is not a botanical word. It looks like a broken form of 'phyllary', which is a synonym of involucral bract. Fix the text normalisation instead of adding a rule.
A corm tunic is the tunic of a corm. The rule loses the corm but the class is right.
Plural of R2429.
'Outer' is a position word. The part is the tunic.
In a fused corolla the lobe is not a separate petal, so petal margin is wrong. The bearer is the corolla lobe (FLOPO_0986006).
Same as R2432. The part is the corolla lobe, not the petal.

match_key: marge des lobes de la corolle
reason: French form of R2432. The part is the corolla lobe.
'With domatia' is a statement that the part is present, not a part name. It needs an entity_presence rule for domatium. A bearer rule would treat 'with domatia' as the bearer.
Same as R2435. 'Avec domaties' states presence and needs an entity_presence rule.
Leaf hair is a leaf trichome.
Plural of R2437.
French form of R2437.
Integument is the ovule integument only when the part is an ovule. In seed descriptions it may mean the seed coat.
Plural of R2440.
French 'tégument' is mostly the seed coat or seed integument. It is the ovule integument only for an ovule. Use a constraint on ovule, or reject the rule.
A tetrad in pollen descriptions is a tetrad of microspores.
A pollen tetrad is a tetrad of microspores.
A pseudo-umbel is an umbel-like inflorescence whose branching is not always cymose. Cyme inflorescence is too specific, so use the generic inflorescence.
Same as R2445.
French form of R2445.
A sterile stamen is a staminode.
A culm sheath is the sheath of a (culm) leaf. It is acceptable, but bamboo culm sheaths are a special organ.
The perigone is the perianth, so the perigone tube is the perianth tube.
French for perianth tube; the class is the existing FLOPO perianth tube.

A scape bract is a bract borne on the flowering axis below the inflorescence branches. That fits the PO definition of inflorescence bract. Some scape bracts are really leaf-like, so this is an approximation.

An epicalyx lobe is a lobe of a fused epicalyx, as in Malvaceae. It is not a separate bract. Mapping it to epicalyx bract loses the lobe and fusion meaning. The epicalyx is the safer bearer, or the rule should be rejected.
Same as R2453: the epicalyx lobe is part of a fused epicalyx, not a free bract.
The exostome is only the outer ring of a double peristome. Mapping it to the whole peristome loses 'outer' and mixes in the endostome. Reject, or add an exostome term.
The outer peristome is only the exostome part of a double peristome. Mapping it to the whole peristome loses that.
Exostome teeth are peristome teeth (PO_0030043, a single lobe of a peristome). They are not the whole peristome.
Endostome cilia are slender filaments between the endostome segments. They are not peristome teeth. No matching PO term exists, so reject.
Cilia of the endostome are filaments, not peristome teeth. No matching PO term exists.
An endostome cilium is a filament, not a peristome tooth. No matching PO term exists.
Rhizoidal tubers are tuber-like propagules on moss rhizoids. PO gemma is a small ball of cells on a thallus, so the two are different structures. Reject.
Rhizoidal tubers are tuber-like propagules on rhizoids, not PO gemmae. Reject.
Rhizoid tubers are tuber-like propagules on rhizoids, not PO gemmae. Reject.
A nectariferous scale is a scale that secretes nectar, which makes it a flower nectary.
A nectary disc is the nectar-secreting disc of the flower, so it is a flower nectary.
Spelling variant of nectary disc.
A nectariferous disc is a nectar-secreting disc, so it is a flower nectary.
Perichaetial leaves are the bracts around the archegonia. 'Perichaetal bract' is the PO term.
Plural of perichaetial leaf; same meaning as the PO perichaetal bract.
Spelling variant of perichaetal bract.

PO_0005656 carries 'gland' as a synonym, but 'basal' is a position. The rule drops it, and it only applies to glands at the base of a leaf, blade or petiole. Use the gland class with a position constraint, or reject.
Same as R2471: the position 'basal' is lost.
French for basal gland; the position 'basal' is lost.

Reticulate veins are leaf lamina veins only when the part is a leaf. Petals and bracts have reticulate veins too, and PO_0020138 is specific to the leaf lamina. 'Reticulate' is a quality of the vein, not part of the bearer.
Plural of reticulate vein; same constraint. The class fits only leaf veins.
Reticulate venation is the network pattern, not a vein. Mapping it to leaf lamina vein loses the pattern, which is the quality 'reticulate'. Handle it as a quality of the leaf venation.
Verticillaster is a listed synonym of cyme inflorescence in the PO lexicon.
Plural of verticillaster; same synonym.

A stigmatic branch is a branch carrying the stigma. Counts such as '2 stigmatic branches' do not mean two stigmas. PO has no stigma-branch term, so the rule loses the 'branch' meaning. Reject, or add a term.
French for stigmatic branch; counts and shape of branches would be recorded as stigma qualities.
Plural of the French stigmatic branch; same problem as R2480.
A stigma branch is a branch, not the stigma itself. Counts and shapes would be misattributed to the stigma.
A winter bud is a dormant bud, such as a turion or hibernaculum. Mapping it to bud loses that. Better to use bud plus a dormancy quality.
Plural of winter bud; the dormant, overwintering sense is lost.
A resting bud is a dormant bud. Mapping it to bud loses the dormancy meaning.
Reticulation is a pattern, a quality of a surface or venation (reticulate), not a part. It is not a leaf lamina vein. Seed or pollen surface reticulation is also covered by the word.
French reticulation is a pattern (a quality), not a vein.
The venation reticulum is the vein network. Mapping it to a single leaf lamina vein loses the network meaning. Reject, or treat it as the quality reticulate venation.
A style branch is a branch of the style, not the style itself. Counts such as '2 style-branches' would be recorded as style counts, and PO has no style-branch term.
Plural of style branch; same problem as R2489.
French for style branch; same problem as R2489.
Interprimary veins are a specific leaf-architecture vein class, lying between primary veins. Mapping them to any leaf lamina vein loses the order.
Plural of interprimary vein; the vein order is lost.
Intersecondary veins are a specific vein class, lying between secondary veins. Mapping them to any leaf lamina vein loses the order.
A secretory canal is a duct or space lined by secretory cells. PO_0005656 is the secretory tissue, so canal counts and sizes would be attached to the tissue.
Plural of secretory canal; the canal is a duct, not the secretory tissue.
French for secretory canal; the canal is a duct, not the tissue.
French plural of secretory canal; the canal is a duct, not the tissue.
A secretory duct is a canal, not the secretory tissue.
The PO comment says the area of alar cells is sometimes called the alar region. Descriptions of the region (colour, size, shape) are descriptions of the alar cells.
Alar regions are patches of enlarged cells at the leaf base in mosses. They are regions made of many cells, not one alar cell. They also lack a clear PO class. Reject rather than map to one cell.
An alar group is a cluster of cells. The target is a single cell type, so the meaning is lost.
An alar area is a region of the leaf base, not a cell. It is not the same as alar cell.
Flowerhead is the usual word for a capitulum in the Asteraceae. The PO lexicon already lists 'head' as a synonym.
'Flower head' is a capitulum in daisy-like plants. In other families it can mean a dense spike or umbel, so apply it only where the head is a true capitulum.
The plural of flowerhead, with the same meaning.
A brood body is a gemma-like vegetative propagule. The word is also used for bulbils and plantlets in flowering plants, and those are not gemmae.
The plural of the previous rule, with the same limit.
A culm sheath is borne on the culm, as in bamboo. It is not a leaf sheath, although it is a modified leaf. No exact PO class was found. Do not map it to leaf sheath.
The plural of the previous rule. A culm sheath is not a leaf sheath.
A median vein is the midvein only when the part is a leaf or leaflet. On other parts, such as a sepal or bract, it would not be a leaf midvein.
'Médiane' is an adjective meaning median. Alone, it does not name a midvein and can mean median lobe, median tooth, median sepal and more.
A pseudostyle is a false style, such as the beak on a fruit or a style-like structure. It is not a true style, so mapping it to style gives it a wrong meaning.
The plural of the previous rule. A pseudostyle is not a style.
Perula, perulae and perule are the botanical words for bud scales, and the lexicon has bud scale as a synonym.
The Latin plural of perula. It means bud scales.
This is an English or French variant of perula. It means bud scale.
Primary divisions of a frond are pinnae. The word is used for other things in other contexts, such as the primary division of a calyx or an inflorescence.
The plural of the previous rule, with the same limit.
This is the French form of the previous rule. It holds for fronds and compound leaves only.
A valve of a capsule is a valve of a fruit, so fruit valve fits.
The plural of capsule valve, with the same meaning.
This is the same as capsule valves, in a different word order.

A false panicle, or pseudopanicle, is an inflorescence that looks like a panicle but is built differently. The target 'inflorescence' is true but loses the panicle-like shape. Use inflorescence with a shape quality, or reject.
This is the French form of false panicle. The same loss of meaning applies.
A spatheate compound panicle is an inflorescence with a spathe and a compound branching pattern. The target keeps neither feature.
Propagula covers many kinds of propagule, such as bulbils, stolons and plantlets. It is a gemma only in bryophytes.
'Asexual propagula' names any vegetative propagule. It is a gemma only in bryophytes.
A needle is a leaf in conifers. In other plants, 'needle' can describe a spine, a crystal (raphide) or a hair.
The plural of needle, with the same limit.
A needle leaf is a leaf. The PO lexicon lists 'needle-like leaf' as a synonym of vascular leaf.
An intersecondary vein is a specific vein class between secondary veins. Leaf lamina vein is true but loses the class. Reject unless a specific vein class exists.
This is the English form of the previous rule. The same loss of the vein class applies.
Leaf blade is a synonym of leaf lamina, so a leaf blade lobe is a leaf lamina lobe.
The plural of leaf blade lobe, with the same meaning.
A lamina lobe is a leaf lamina lobe.
'Phyllaryllary' is a typing error for 'phyllary'. Phyllary is a synonym of involucral bract, so the target is right, but the key is garbled. Use the key 'phyllary' instead.
The singular of propagula. It is a gemma only in bryophytes.
A bisexual flower has both stamens and pistils. The target 'flower' drops this sexual condition. Use flower with a quality such as bisexual.
A hermaphrodite flower is bisexual. The target 'flower' loses that.
A perfect flower is bisexual. The target 'flower' loses that.
The symbol ☿ means hermaphrodite. The target 'flower' loses that.
A vegetative part is any non-reproductive part, such as leaves, stems and roots. It is broader than the vegetative shoot system, which excludes roots.
The plural of vegetative part. It has the same problem.
A female inflorescence is pistillate only in plants with separate sexes. The PO lexicon lists it as a synonym, so the rule is mostly right.
The plural of female inflorescence, a listed synonym of pistillate inflorescence.
This is the French form of female inflorescence.
The phrase means the inflorescences of the female flowers, which are pistillate inflorescences.
An aristate scale is a scale with an awn, here a pappus scale. 'Aristate' is a shape quality, so the key names a quality plus a part. Map the part to pappus element and the quality to aristate.
The plural of aristate scale. 'Aristate' should be a quality, not part of the bearer.
Pappus scales are a kind of pappus element. PO lists 'pappus scale' as a synonym.
PO lists 'sucker' as a synonym of root-borne shoot system.
A root sucker is a shoot that grows from a root.
A false umbel (pseudo-umbel) is an umbel-like cyme.
French 'fausse ombelle' is the same as 'false umbel'.
Plural of 'fausse ombelle'.
French 'fleur' means flower.
French 'fleurs' means flowers.
PO lists 'lacunae' as a synonym of plant anatomical space.
PO lists 'lacuna' as a synonym of plant anatomical space.
A flowering branch is a branch. The flowering state is lost, but the bearer is right.
Plural of 'flowering branch'. The bearer is a branch.
French for 'flowering branch'. The bearer is a branch.
Plural of 'rameau florifère'. The bearer is a branch.
'leave' is a typo for 'leaves'. Involucral leaves are involucral bracts.
'pedicelk' is a typo for 'pedicel'.
'Juice' of a fruit is fruit juice, not plant sap. The rule is only safe for vegetative parts.
Herbage is the leafy above-ground shoot, so shoot system fits.
'foliol' is a misspelling of 'foliole', which means leaflet.
Minor veins are veins of the leaf lamina. The vein order is lost, but the bearer is right.
Plural of 'minor vein'.
PO lists 'petiolar gland' as a synonym of extrafloral nectary.
French for 'petiolar gland'.
This looks like a typo or OCR error for 'inflorescence'. I could not confirm the original text.
A cilium is a marginal hair, which is a trichome.
PO lists 'gland' as a synonym of portion of secretory tissue. It is the only PO term for glands.
The word 'racemose' (raceme-like arrangement of cymes) is lost. A racemose cyme is not a plain cyme. Better to treat it as a cyme inflorescence with a racemose quality, or reject the rule.
Plural of 'racemose cyme'. The racemose arrangement is lost.
'spicate' is an adjective meaning spike-like. It describes the form of an inflorescence and is not a bearer. It should be a quality of the inflorescence.
PO lists 'pitcher' as a synonym of vascular leaf.
Plural of 'pitcher'.
The coat of a bulb is its tunic.
Plural of 'bulb coat'.
A bulb tunic is a tunic.
'outer coat' is also used for seeds, fruits and stems (testa, pericarp). It means tunic only on bulbs and corms.
Microscales are small scale-like trichomes, for example peltate scales.
Plural of 'microscale'.
PO gives hypophysis as a synonym of sporangium base, which holds for moss capsules only. In seed plants it means an embryo cell, and apophysis can mean part of a cone scale.
Plural of 'hypophysis'. Only valid for moss sporophytes.
'apophysis' means sporangium base in mosses. In conifer cones it is the exposed part of the cone scale.
Receptacle scales (chaff, paleae) of Asteraceae are flower bracts. PO lists 'chaff' as a synonym.
Plural of 'receptacle scale'.
French for 'receptacle scale'.
PO lists 'chaff' as a synonym of flower bract. A chaff scale is a receptacle bract.
A pseudospikelet is not a true spikelet, so the 'pseudo' meaning is lost. Mapping it to spikelet states something false about the structure.
Same as 'pseudospikelet'. A pseudo-spikelet is not a spikelet.
'pseudaril' is a variant of 'pseudaril/pseudarillus', an aril-like outgrowth, so arilloid fits.
A pseudarillus is an arilloid.
A false aril is an arilloid.
A cyathophyll is the bract that subtends a cyathium, so it is an inflorescence bract.
The bracts of a cyathium (Euphorbia) are bracts of a reduced inflorescence, so inflorescence bract fits.
Cyathophylls are the bracts under a cyathium, so inflorescence bract fits.
An innovation is a new shoot from an axillary bud at the base of the plant (grasses, sedges, bamboos). PO has axillary shoot system for this.
Plural of R2603.
French 'loge' means locule.
Plural of 'loge' means locules.
A soral line is a linear sorus or a line of sori in ferns. The sorus class carries the statement.
Plural of R2607.
The vein network of a leaf is its vascular system.
Network of veinlets in a leaf is the leaf lamina vascular system.
A vein reticulum is a net of leaf veins.
A venation network is a net of leaf veins.
A fruit stalk is the fruit pedicel. It is occasionally the stalk of the whole infructescence, but that is rare.
Plural of R2613.
A fruiting pedicel is the pedicel of the fruit.
The main nerve is the midrib or a primary vein. Leaf lamina vein is a safe parent class (the midrib is leaf midvein PO_0020139, a kind of vein).
Main nerves are the primary veins. Leaf lamina vein fits.
A leaflet lobe is a lobe of a leaflet blade, i.e. a leaf lamina lobe.
Plural of R2618.
A pinna lobe is a lobe of the pinna blade.
A pinnule lobe is a lobe of the pinnule blade.
A corona scale is a scale of the corona, not a lobe. The floral corona class (FLOPO_0985020) keeps the meaning without inventing a lobe.
A nervule is a small vein, so leaf lamina vein fits.
A French 'nerville' is a veinlet.
Plural of R2623.
A lateral pinna is a pinna. The side position is only a qualifier.
French 'penne latérale' is a lateral pinna.
'Upper lip' is also used for the calyx (Lamiaceae, Fabaceae) and for the orchid labellum, so it is the corolla lip only when the part is the corolla.
French 'lèvre supérieure' is also used for the calyx and the labellum, so it fits only for the corolla.
Spathe valves are the bract-like parts of a spathe (e.g. the two bracts of an iris spathe). PO lists spathe as a synonym of inflorescence bract.
Same as R2630.
A secondary pinnule is a pinnule. The order is only a qualifier.
A ventral sporophyll is a sporophyll (e.g. Selaginella). The position is a qualifier.
French 'sporophylle ventral' is a ventral sporophyll.
A pedoconnective is a stalk-like extension of the anther connective, so connective is its nearest PO class.
French spelling of R2635.
Plural of R2635.
'Disk' is a spelling variant of 'disc'.
A subumbel is a small or reduced umbel.
'Subumbellate' means only umbel-like. The inflorescence is not an umbel, and the class would claim it is. Use the inflorescence as bearer with a value 'subumbellate', or reject it.
PO lists pappus awn as a synonym of pappus element.
A corona filament is a filament (e.g. Passiflora), not a lobe. The corona class fits better.
Plural of R2642.
'Filament of corona' is a filament, not a lobe. The corona class fits better.
A bulbel is a small bulb or bulblet, a PO synonym.
A central floret is a disk flower only in an Asteraceae head. In a grass spikelet or an umbel it is not.
A central flower is a disk flower only in an Asteraceae head. In a cyme it is just the terminal flower.
A floret lobe is a lobe of the floret's corolla.
Nervation is the pattern of veins, i.e. the vascular system of the leaf, not one vascular bundle.
Venation is the pattern of veins, i.e. the vascular system of the leaf, not one vascular bundle.
Rhachis internode in grass and sedge spikes is the inflorescence axis internode. Leaf rachis internodes are rare.
Same as R2651: rachis internode is the inflorescence axis internode.
A rachis joint is the internode between two nodes of a spike rachis, as in grasses. It is the breaking point of the axis.
Same as R2653, with the rhachis spelling.
A fasciclode is a bundle of staminodes, not a single staminode. Mapping it to staminode loses the fascicle. Reject unless a fascicle term exists.
Same as R2655: a fasciclodium is a fascicle of staminodes, not one staminode.
Leaf auricle is the leaf sheath auricle only in grasses. In other plants, such as stipular, Rubus or fern auricles, the leaf base or lamina bears it.
Bare auricles also occur on stipules, corollas, bracts, pinnae and fruits. The match to PO_0020106 holds only for grass leaf and sheath contexts.
Sheath auricles are the leaf sheath auricles.
A monochasium is a cyme with one lateral branch per node. PO cyme inflorescence is the nearest class, and it also covers dichasium.
Plural of monochasium (R2660).
A spelling variant of monochasium (R2660).
A monochasial cyme is a cyme.
The limen in Passiflora is a membranous ring or cup around the base of the androgynophore, inside the coronas. It is not the corona itself. Reject unless a limen class is made.
The inner corona is only the inner part of the corona. Mapping it to floral corona loses that. Use only if no inner/outer corona classes exist.
A dyad is mostly a pair of pollen grains, or a pair of flowers or spikelets. It is not a cyme. The glossary lists it as unmapped.
Plural of dyad (R2666). Dyads are mostly pollen units, so this is not a cyme.
French dyade is a pair of pollen grains or flowers, not a cyme.
A submarginal vein runs close inside the margin of the lamina, which fits the intramarginal vein.
Plural of R2669.
French equivalent of submarginal vein (R2669).
Plural of R2671.
Sillon is a groove. PO canal lists groove and furrow as synonyms.
Plural of R2673.
Perigonial leaves are perigonial bracts only in bryophytes. In seed plants, a perigonial leaf is a tepal.
A protonemal flap is a flap-like outgrowth on the protonema, not the protonema itself. Mapping to protonema loses the part.
Same as R2676, with the other spelling.
A petiolar sheath is the sheath of a leaf at the petiole base, which maps to the leaf sheath.
Same as R2678.
French 'flore' normally means a flora, as in the book. It does not mean flower, which is 'fleur'.
'-flore' is a suffix, as in 'pauciflore' or '3-flore', meaning 'flowered'. It describes the number or kind of flowers, so it does not name a flower. Handle it as a count rule.
'-flores' is the plural suffix form ('multiflores', '3-flores'). It describes flower number, so it does not name a flower part.
The axis of a panicle is the inflorescence axis.
Plural of R2683.
The panicle rachis is the main inflorescence axis. PO lists inflorescence rachis as a synonym.
A longitudinal nerve is a vein, and PO lists vein as a synonym of vascular bundle. 'Longitudinal' is a direction and could be a separate quality.
The blade is the expanded part of a bract. Sedge and grass bracts have a sheath and a blade, so a quality of the blade would be wrongly put on the whole bract.
Same as R2687: the lamina is a part of the bract, not the whole bract.
A reduced stamen may still be fertile and just small. A staminode is sterile, so the target says more than the words do.
Same as R2689: reduced does not mean sterile.
Hyalodermis is the outer layer of hyaline cells, for example in the stem cortex of Sphagnum or on orchid roots. It is not a stem epidermis in general.
Same as R2691, with the other spelling.
Flower head is a standard name for a capitulum, and PO lists 'head' as a synonym.
Bulbils are the plural of bulbil, which is the FLOPO class.
French plural of bulbille.
French singular of bulbil.
Veinlets are the smallest veins and also occur in sepals, petals and bracts. Only for leaves does the target hold, and the smallest-order meaning is lost.
The lower surface of a leaf is the abaxial side of the lamina, covered by its abaxial epidermis.
French 'face inférieure' can be the underside of any organ. It is the leaf abaxial surface only when the bearer is a leaf, lamina, limbe or leaflet.
Lower leaf surface is the abaxial surface of the leaf lamina.
An involucrenule is a small involucre, and PO involucre is the closest class. Whether it should be a separate part is doubtful.
A leaf tooth is a tooth of the leaf margin. This matches PO leaf lamina tooth.
This is the plural of leaf tooth. PO lists it as a synonym.
The French 'dents des feuilles' means leaf teeth.
A beard is a tuft of hairs on a petal, staminode or lip, as in Iris and Penstemon. In cereals, a beard means the awns, so the word has two meanings.
The key includes 'present', but the target is only the midvein. The rule loses the presence quality. An entity_presence rule is the right kind.
The hypanthium is a fused tube of sepals, petals and stamens. Its lobes are often sepals but can be petals or epicalyx. Mapping them to calyx lobe asserts sepals.
Same as R2707. A hypanthial lobe is not always a calyx lobe.
Same as R2707. Lobes of the hypanthium are not always calyx lobes.
An awn-point is the tip of an awn, or a short awn-like point on a glume or lemma. It is not the whole awn.
Same as R2710. 'Awn point' means the tip, not the whole awn.
Same as R2710, in the plural.
PO sporangium wall fits only a bryophyte or fern capsule. In flowering plants the capsule is a fruit, and its wall is the fruit wall (pericarp).
Same as R2713, in the plural.
Brood bodies are gemmae.
This is the plural of brood-body, which means gemmae.
In Meliaceae and similar families, a staminal cup is a fused filament tube, usually short and wide. Staminal tube is the closest class.
Same as R2717, in the plural.
Same as R2717. A stamen cup is a fused staminal tube.
Secondary leaf vein is a leaf class. Secondary nerves also occur on bracts, sepals and petals, where it would be wrong.
A resin gland is a gland, and PO gland is the secretory tissue class. The resin content is lost but the bearer is right.
Same as R2721, in the plural.
A compound cyme is a cyme inflorescence. 'Compound' is a branching quality and is lost.
Same as R2723, in the plural.
The French 'cyme composée' means compound cyme.
The French 'cymes composées' is the plural of compound cyme.
Corona appendages (horns, scales, teeth) sit on or are outgrowths of the corona lobes. They are not the lobes themselves.
Same as R2727, in the plural.
PO lists chaff as a synonym of flower bract. In Asteraceae, chaff means receptacle scales, which are bracts.
This is the plural of chaff, which PO lists as a synonym of flower bract.
Receptacular chaff means the paleae, which are receptacle bracts.
An anther lobe is a theca, which is half of the anther.
This is the plural of anther lobe, which means thecae.
The urn is the spore-bearing body of a moss capsule. Sporangium is the nearest class.
The French 'fleurs hermaphrodites' means bisexual flowers. The rule loses the sexual condition. It should be flower plus a bisexual quality.
The rule loses 'hermaphrodite', which is the sexual condition. It should be flower plus a bisexual quality.
An ovulate cone is a megasporangiate strobilus. PO lists it as a synonym.
This is the plural of ovulate cone. PO lists it as a synonym.
A glandular dot is a gland, often a translucent oil gland. The gland class is the nearest.
Same as R2739, in the plural.
A gland dot is a gland.
Same as R2741, in the plural.
'Phyllaryl' is not a botanical term. It looks like a truncated 'phyllary' or 'phyllarial'. A rule on the fragment risks false matches.
'Circular' is a shape quality and the rule drops it. The bearer is a gland and the shape should be a separate quality.
Same as R2744. The circular shape of the glands is lost.
A tiller is a basal axillary shoot in grasses. PO lists it as a synonym.
PO lists vein as a synonym of vascular bundle. The rule fits veins of any part.
PO lists dichasium as a synonym of cyme inflorescence. 'Compound' is lost but the bearer is right.
A sprout is a young shoot. Shoot system is the nearest class.
The rule loses 'adventitious', which is the origin of the shoot. It should be shoot system plus an adventitious quality.
The blade is the lamina, so the blade apex is the leaf apex. PO lists 'leaf lamina apex' as a synonym.
'leaf lamina apex' is a PO synonym of leaf apex.
French for the apex of the lamina, which is the leaf apex.
The dorsal sepal is one particular sepal, mostly in orchids. Mapping it to 'sepal' would spread its qualities to all sepals. It needs a position-specific class, or the rule should be dropped.
Same as 'dorsal sepal'. The position (dorsal) is lost.
Inner petals are a distinct whorl or set, for example in Annonaceae. Mapping them to 'petal' loses which petals the quality applies to.

A sac on the lip (labellum) is a pouch, not a spur. A spur is a tubular or conical extension, and a sac is a different structure. The PO 'petal spur' class does not fit, and a labellum with a saccate shape would be a better fit.
Same as 'lip sac'. A sac is not a spur.
Outer petals are a specific set (for example Annonaceae outer versus inner petals). The position is lost.
In grasses the sessile spikelet differs from the pedicelled one. Mapping to 'spikelet' loses that contrast and makes the statement ambiguous.
A staminal sheath is the tube formed by fused filaments (monadelphous), which is the staminal tube.
A stamen sheath is the same structure as the staminal tube.
Endostome processes (segments and cilia) are the inner peristome. Peristome teeth are mainly the exostome. The two are not the same structure.
Spore sac is a common name for sporangium. PO lists 'spore case' and 'spore capsule' as synonyms.
The receptacular tube (floral cup) is the hypanthium.
The axis of the spikelet is the rachilla.
'Parallel vein' describes the venation pattern, which is a quality of the leaf, not a vascular bundle. It should be a leaf vein with a parallel-venation quality.
Same as 'parallel vein'. It is a venation pattern, not the part.
Same as 'parallel vein'. It is a venation pattern, not the part.
The principal nerve is the main (primary) vein or midvein of the leaf. 'Vascular bundle' is far too general. Use primary leaf vein, or leaf midvein PO_0020139 for a single midrib.
The principal vein is the primary leaf vein or midvein, not any vascular bundle.
A root hair is a root hair cell, a single-cell outgrowth.
Plural of 'root hair'.
The seed scar is the hilum, the scar where the seed was attached.
French for 'seed scar', which is the hilum.
Intercostal veins run between the costal (secondary) veins, which makes them tertiary veins in leaf architecture.
Plural of 'intercostal vein'.
Used alone, 'intercostals' also means the intercostal zones or tissue between veins, mainly in grasses. It is not always a vein.
A stipular sheath is a sheath made of fused stipules, which is the ochrea.
A stipular tube is the same as the ochrea.
'present' is a quality (presence) and is lost when only the bearer is mapped. This should be an entity_presence rule on 'colleters'.
'Calycine' says where the colleters are (on the calyx). Plain 'colleter' loses this. It needs a calyx container, or the rule should be dropped.
A misspelling of 'inflorescence'.
A stipitate (stalked) gland is usually a glandular trichome. The generic 'gland' loses the stalk. Check against the glandular trichome class.
Plural of 'stipitate gland'. Same issue.
'aerial root' is a PO synonym of shoot-borne root.
Plural of 'aerial root'.
French for 'aerial root'.
A dichasium is a PO synonym of cyme inflorescence. A dichasial cyme is a cyme.
Plural of 'dichasial cyme'.
'Discoid' (disc-shaped) is a shape of the gland and is lost. The generic secretory tissue class says nothing of the gland type.
Plural of 'discoid gland'. Same issue.
'Perfect' means bisexual, which is a quality of the flower. A stamen is not 'perfect' in that sense. It is not a kind of stamen.
Same as 'perfect stamen'. It describes the flower's sexuality, not a type of stamen.
A stalked gland is a glandular trichome with a stalk. The stalk is lost when mapped to generic gland tissue.
Plural of 'stalked gland'. Same issue.
It is a cyme, but the umbel-like shape is lost. The shape should be kept as a quality.
It is a cyme, but the umbel-like shape is lost. The shape should be kept as a quality.

'present' is a presence quality, not part of the bearer name. A hair-point is an apical hair tip, and it is not the same as the leaf apex. It needs an entity_presence rule on a hair-point, or a hairy-tipped apex.
Umbel rays are the first-order branches of the umbel. PO gives 'first order inflorescence branch' as a synonym of second order inflorescence axis.

Rays are the primary branches of an umbel (the PO synonym 'first order inflorescence branch' fits). The word 'rays' also means ray florets of Asteraceae and wood rays, so it needs an inflorescence context.
Umbel rays are the primary inflorescence branches.
A gametangium is an archegonium or antheridium of bryophytes and ferns. In flowering plant floras 'sex organs' means stamens and pistil, or the androecium and gynoecium.
Same as 'sex organ': it means stamens and pistil in seed plants, not gametangia.
'Organes sexuels' means stamens and pistil in French floras, not gametangia.
As a bearer, 'pubescence' is the hair covering, which is the indumentum.
A reddish-brown hair covering is an indumentum. The colour is a separate quality.
The order 'secondary' is lost. Statements would mix with the plain bracts of the primary axis. Bracteole is only a synonym when the bract is on a secondary axis.
The order 'secondary' is lost, as for the singular.
The order 'secondaires' is lost, as for the English rule.
A colpus is a pollen aperture. PO 'canal' is a groove or channel of an organ, which is a different thing. Pollen apertures need a pollen aperture class, not canal.
Colpus is a pollen aperture, not a canal or groove of an organ.
'Colpé' means 'having colpi', which is a quality word and not a part. It is also a pollen aperture, not a canal.
Perigone (perianth) segments are tepals.
Perigone segments are tepals.
'Segments du périgone' are tepals.
The seed scale of a conifer cone is the ovuliferous scale, which is a PO synonym of megasporophyll.
A fruiting scale is a cone scale of a conifer, or a scale in fruit in Carex or Atriplex. It is not the grass fertile lemma. For a conifer cone, PO_0009027 would fit, but the word is ambiguous.
The galea is only the hooded upper lip, and in orchids a hood made of sepals and petals. The class 'corolla lip' loses 'upper' and 'hooded', and does not fit the orchid sense.
The sex 'pistillate' is lost. The spike inflorescence class would take statements about all spikes, and not only those with female flowers.
Calicle (calyculus) is a PO synonym of epicalyx.
Disk scales are scale-like parts or segments of the disc, not the whole floral disc. The meaning also varies by family, so it should not be mapped to the whole disc.
'Lip' is either the orchid labellum or the corolla lip (see the rejected 'lip limb'). Without the family the labellum lobe may be wrong. It is correct only for orchids.
The epichile is the distal part of the orchid labellum, so its lobes are labellum lobes.
'Stipe' is the stalk of a fern frond, a pappus, a pollinarium or a gynophore. The PO class 'stalk' loses whose stalk it is. It needs the organ.
'Stipes' is a stalk of an unnamed organ, so the stalk class loses the organ.
The stipe of a pollinarium is the stalk of that one organ. The generic stalk class loses 'pollinarium'. It needs a container rule.
A stem scale may be a scale leaf (cataphyll) or an epidermal scale (trichome, as in ferns). Mapping it to a trichome is correct only for some plants.
Rhizome scales are usually scale leaves, or epidermal scales in ferns. The two senses cannot be told apart, so the trichome class is doubtful.
Same as 'stem scale': scale leaves versus epidermal scales.
Secondary veins are secondary leaf veins. The 'per side' count is handled by the counted-part pattern.
Lateral nerves are secondary veins in Malesian floras.
Perianth members may be sepals and petals in a differentiated perianth. Tepal is right only for an undifferentiated perianth.
Pleiochasium is a PO synonym of cyme inflorescence.
Plural of pleiochasium.
A twig is a PO synonym of branch. 'Leafy' only describes the twig.
Plural of leafy twig, same as the singular.
A branchlet is a PO synonym of branch.
A sheath scar is the scar left by a leaf sheath. A culm sheath is a modified leaf.
A culm sheath scar is the scar of a culm sheath (a modified leaf).
'Lip' may be the corolla lip or the orchid labellum, and the median position is lost. It is correct only for orchids.
'Lip' may be the corolla lip or the orchid labellum, and the median position is lost.
The labellum is named, so the median lobe of the labellum is a labellum lobe. This follows the earlier note on rejected generic lobes.
Connecting veins are cross-veins between the secondaries, a PO synonym of tertiary leaf vein.
The position 'inner' is lost. Inner and outer phyllaries often differ, and statements would mix.
The position 'inner' is lost. Inner and outer phyllaries often differ.
Coronal filaments (for example in Passiflora) are thread-like parts of the corona. They are not corona lobes, which are the lobes of an asclepiad or daffodil corona.
Coronal filaments are not corona lobes.
Same part as spathe limb, written with a hyphen.
The labellum is named, so its lateral lobe is a labellum lobe. This follows the earlier note on rejected generic lobes.
A lateral lobe of the labellum is a labellum lobe. Position is not kept, as with inner/outer tepal.
French form of R2851.

An ochreola is a small sheath at the base of a pedicel or flower cluster, made of fused bracts (Polygonaceae). An ochrea is the stipular sheath around the stem node. R2872 already maps 'ochreole' to inflorescence bract, so the two rules disagree.
Plural of R2853: ochreola is not ochrea.
Spelling variant of ochreola. See R2853.
Plural of the ocreola variant. See R2853.
The seed cone scale bears the ovules, so megasporophyll is a fair functional match. It is not strictly homologous in conifers, so confidence is low.
Hyphenated variant of R2857.
Plural of R2857.
'Knee' alone also means a bent node or geniculate part in grasses and bamboos. It is a pneumatophore only when it is a root knee.
Plural of R2860, with the same ambiguity.
A knee root is an upward-growing respiratory root, which is a pneumatophore.
The carpocephalum is the female receptacle of Marchantiales, which is the archegoniophore.
Singular of R2863.
The lateral nerves arising from the midrib (the primary vein) are the secondary leaf veins. The word 'primary' only means the main laterals.
Plural of R2865.

A flower bract subtends a perianth. A staminate scale in catkins (Betulaceae, Casuarina, Carex) is a bract or glume subtending a naked or reduced male flower, so inflorescence bract is closer. In conifers it is a microsporophyll.
Plural of R2867.

A perianth cup is a cup made of fused perianth parts. A hypanthium is receptacle or axis tissue that carries the perianth and stamens, so the two are not the same. Perianth tube or calyx tube is closer.
An umbellate raceme is a raceme with an umbel-like look. The base class is acceptable, though the umbellate detail is lost.
The fruiting axis is the axis of the infructescence.
The ochreole (ochreola) of Polygonaceae is a bract-derived sheath on the inflorescence or pedicel.
Hyphenated spelling of spathe tube.
The leaf face is the leaf surface (upper or lower), and the lamina epidermis is the surface layer. Phyllodes and needles are the exceptions.
Plural of R2874.
'Faces' alone also means the faces of a petal, seed, valve, glume or achene.
The anther theca is the half-anther with two pollen sacs. The French spelling without an accent is the same word.
French 'thèque de l'anthère' is the anther theca.
Plural of R2878.
In gymnosperm ovules the pollen chamber is a cavity at the top of the nucellus that receives pollen. That is not a pollen sac. It is a pollen sac only in anthers.
The 'loge pollinique' is the anther locule, which is the pollen sac.
Plural of R2881.
A polychasium is a compound cyme with many lateral branches. The cyme class is the nearest existing term.
The PO comment treats the alar region as the area of alar cells. The loss of 'region' is minor.
Direct match.
A cone scale is a sporophyll, or sporophyll-like, in cones. It is homologous only in some groups, so confidence is limited.
Plural of R2886.
Stigmatic rays are the ray-like lobes of the stigma, for example in Papaver.
Plural of R2888.
Variant of R2888.
The floret tube is the corolla tube in Asteraceae and similar heads. In grasses the floret has no such tube.
Plural of R2891.
A fertile bract is a bract that bears flowers. 'Fertile' is dropped, as with inner and outer tepal.
French form of R2893.
Plural of R2894.
The inner tepal is a tepal. The review of 2026-11-13 already mapped 'inner tepal' to tepal.
French form of R2896.
Plural of R2897.
A male floret is a staminate flower (a staminate floret in Poaceae and Asteraceae).
A pappus hair is a bristle-like pappus element.
The stalk of a sporocarp (Marsilea, Azolla) is a stalk.
The peduncle of a sporocarp is its stalk, so this maps to stalk.
The pedicels of an umbellet are the flower stalks, so this maps to flower pedicel.
'Fall' means an outer tepal only in Iris and its relatives. Elsewhere it means leaf fall or the season, so the rule needs a flower or perianth context.
The endostome is the inner peristome of mosses, so its teeth are peristome teeth. The rule loses the inner/outer distinction, which is acceptable for a bearer.
Same word as 'disc gland', with a hyphen.
An epigynous gland is a nectary on top of an inferior ovary, which is an epigynous disc. It is not a general disc gland, and the match is doubtful, so reject it.
Throat scales are scales in the corolla throat, as in Boraginaceae. They are the same structure as faucal scales, which map to corolline corona.
Faucal scales (fornices) of the corolla throat map to corolline corona. The review of 2026-11-14 already said so.
The stalk of a leaflet is the petiolule.
'Areola' is an areole bud in cacti and Euphorbia. In leaf venation and in lichens it means a small area or space, so it must not be matched everywhere.
'Areole' is an areole bud in cacti. It also means the small area between veins in leaf venation.
The exostome is the outer peristome, and its teeth are the peristome teeth. 'Filament' is the term for the inner endostome processes, so this mixes the two rows. Reject it.
A green cell is a chlorophyll-bearing cell, which is a chlorenchyma cell (for example the chlorocysts in Sphagnum).
In sedges, spikelet scales are bracts that each subtend a flower, so flower bract fits. In grasses the glumes are not floral bracts.
This is the French form of 'spikelet scale'. It fits flower bract in sedges, but not for grass glumes.
Areolar glands of cacti are extrafloral nectaries.
Areole glands of cacti are extrafloral nectaries.
The culm is the stem of a grass or sedge, so a culm internode is a stem internode.
Plural of 'culm internode'.
A nucule is a small nut. It is a mericarp only in schizocarpic fruits such as Boraginaceae and Lamiaceae. In Chara it is the oogonium.
Plural of 'nucule'. The same limits apply: it is a mericarp only in schizocarpic fruits.
Sclerotic granules are small groups of stone cells. Sclerenchyma is the whole tissue, so the mapping loses the 'cluster' part of the meaning. It is acceptable only as a loose approximation.
Singular of 'sclerotic granule'. A granule is a cluster of stone cells, not the tissue, so the same limit applies.
Stone cells are sclereids, which are sclerenchyma. A cluster of them is a portion of sclerenchyma.
Grit cells are stone cells (sclereids), so a cluster of them is a portion of sclerenchyma.

'Lip' is either the orchid labellum or a corolla lip. The lip class (FLOPO_0985017) fits the corolla lip. Labellum lobe fits only when the part is an orchid labellum, as the 'lip limb' rejection shows.
A branchlet of an inflorescence is a higher-order inflorescence axis.
This is the same as 'inflorescence branchlet', written the other way round.
A cell of the central strand is a cell, not the strand. Mapping it to central strand loses the 'cell' part.
A bract-like sheath is a sheath, not a scale leaf. A bract-like sheath is not a cataphyll.
A sheathing bract is a bract, not a scale leaf (cataphyll). It should map to bract.
A sterile bract is a bract that bears no flower. It is not a scale leaf, so it should map to bract.
'Fruited' is an adjective meaning 'bearing fruit' or 'in fruit'. It is a state of the plant, not a part, so it is not a bearer.
Transverse veins join the secondary veins, which makes them tertiary veins. 'Cross-vein' is already a PO synonym.
An anthelodium is an anthela-type inflorescence (Juncaceae, Cyperaceae).
Same word as 'leaf scar', with a hyphen.
A lobe of the flower is a lobe of its perianth, so it maps to perianth lobe.
'Punctation' means a pattern of dots or pits. It is a quality (punctate), not a secretory tissue.
A costula is the secondary rachis (midrib) of a pinnule in ferns, not a vascular bundle. No existing class fits, so reject it.
A primary pinnule is a pinnule. The rank is lost but the part is the same.
The stipe of a tegula is a stalk. Low confidence, because 'tegula' is a rare word.
Epicalyx scales are the bracts of the epicalyx.
Plural of 'epicalyx scale'.
A stem leaf is a cauline leaf.
A stem leaf is a cauline leaf.
Plural of 'stem-leaf', which is a cauline leaf.
Plural of 'stem leaf', which is a cauline leaf.
Perianth scales are reduced tepals, as in Cyperaceae and Juncaceae.
Plural of 'perianth scale', which is a reduced tepal.
Perianth scales (Cyperaceae, Amaranthaceae) are reduced perianth parts. They are not always undifferentiated tepals. Perianth (PO_0009058) is the safer bearer.
Gametophore branch is a bryophyte term. 'Branch stem' in flora texts means an ordinary branch of a vascular plant.
Same as R2952. The plural of 'branch stem' means ordinary branches, not gametophore branches.
A rudimentary ovary in a functionally staminate flower is a pistillode (a sterile pistil).
French 'rudiment d'ovaire' is the same concept as R2954.
'Rudimentary ovary' is the same concept as R2954.
A receptacular tube is a floral cup or tube bearing the perianth and stamens, which is a hypanthium.
The stigmatic surface is the receptive part of the stigma. Qualities such as papillose describe the stigma.
French 'plage stigmatique' means the stigmatic area, which is the stigma.
Plural of R2959.
A stigmatic zone is the receptive stigma region.
French 'zone stigmatique' means the stigmatic zone, as in R2961.
Interlacunar bundles are vascular bundles lying between air lacunae (Cyperaceae, Typha, aquatic plants).
Plural of R2963.
A pseudo-aril is an arilloid, a fleshy outgrowth of the seed that is not a true aril.
Same as R2965, without the hyphen.
The valves are parts of the spathe (Musa, Araceae, Commelina). Mapping them to the spathe puts valve qualities on the whole spathe. A valve-of-spathe part is needed, or the rule should be dropped.
Same as R2967. 'Valve of spathe' is a part of the spathe, not the spathe itself.
A culm sheath is a modified leaf sheath (bamboos, grasses), so its auricle is a leaf sheath auricle.
Hyphenated variant of R2969.
Word-order variant of R2969.

The epimatium is the fleshy aril-like outgrowth of the ovuliferous scale that covers the seed in Podocarpaceae. It is not the megasporophyll, which is the scale itself. No good existing PO term was found.
Plural of R2972. Epimatia are fleshy seed coverings, not megasporophylls.

target: leaf lamina vein + palmate venation quality
reason: 'Palmate' says how the veins are arranged (venation pattern). The rule drops this and keeps only 'vein'.

target: leaf lamina vein + palmate venation quality
