reason: Same as R2974: the palmate arrangement is lost.

target: leaf lamina vein + palmate venation quality
reason: Same as R2974: the palmate arrangement is lost. 'Nerves' means veins.
PO_0006018 is the adaxial epidermis of a leaf. Other organs (petal, phyllode, stem) also have adaxial epidermis.
The target is leaf-only. Adaxial epidermis on other parts would be mislabelled.
'Upper epidermal layer' is a synonym of the leaf adaxial epidermis only when the part is a leaf.
A pod valve is a valve of a dehiscent fruit, which is a fruit valve.
Same as R2980.
French 'valve de la gousse' means pod valve.
Staminal scales are usually scale-like appendages or nectaries at the stamen base (Santalaceae, Ranunculaceae, Rhamnaceae), not the stamen itself. The microsporophyll reading holds only in conifers.
French 'écaille staminale' is ambiguous. It is a microsporophyll only for conifer cones, so it is doubtful for a general rule.
An accessory bundle is an additional vascular bundle.
Same as R2985.
A racemose branch of a panicle or compound inflorescence is a higher-order inflorescence axis. 'Inflorescence branch' is a synonym.
A racemiform branch is a branch of the inflorescence, as in R2987.
A leaf fascicle is a short shoot bearing a leaf cluster (Pinus, Larix, Berberis).
An axillary leaf fascicle is a short shoot in a leaf axil.
A leaf cluster can be a rosette or a terminal tuft, not necessarily on a short shoot. Only 'fascicle' reliably means a short shoot.
The gynostegial corona (Apocynaceae) is a corona derived from the stamens, so it is a staminal corona.
Latin/French 'corona staminea' means staminal corona.
'Perigyn' is a Carex term for the perigynium (the sac around the pistillate flower).
French 'périgyne' is mostly an adjective meaning perigynous (flower type). It is the perigynium only as a noun for sedges.
The target is a shoot-borne root spine, a palm term (Acanthorhiza). 'Root thorn' can mean any spine-like root, so the target is too specific.
Same as R2996. The target is specific to shoot-borne roots (palms).
Plural of R2996, with the same problem.
Laminal papillae are papillae of the leaf epidermis, which are leaf papilla cells (bryophytes).
'Lamina papillae' means papillae on the leaf lamina, as in R2999.
An appendage of the protonema is a part of it (e.g. a branch or bud), not the protonema itself. Reject, or use a part class if one exists.
Same as R3001: an appendage of the protonema is not the protonema.
Hydatode is a spelling variant of hydathode (water pore).
Hydatode is a spelling variant of hydathode.
Plural of hydathode.
A sinus is a leaf sinus only on a leaf or lamina. Basal sinus can also mean a sinus of a calyx or corolla.
Basal leaf sinus is the sinus at the base of the leaf blade, so it is a leaf sinus.
Gynostegial column is the gynostegium (Apocynaceae), the fused stamens and style head.
Gynostegium column is the gynostegium.

A resin pocket is a secretory cavity, but PO_0005656 'portion of secretory tissue' has gland as a synonym and is not a cavity. Use only where the existing rules already treat cavities as secretory tissue. Otherwise reject.
A resin cavity is a secretory space, not the tissue itself. Same doubt as R3010.
Plural of resin pocket, same doubt as R3010.
A sporangiaster is a sterile, sporangium-like structure of some fungi and ferns, not a spore-bearing sporangium. Mapping it to sporangium loses this meaning.
Plural of sporangiaster, same problem as R3013.
A modified sporangium is a special kind (e.g. a sporangiophore or a sterile type). The word 'modified' is lost. Reject.

The palea of a grass floret is a floret bract (a lemma-like part), not an inflorescence bract. The palea synonym in PO_0009054 is about the corn husk. Pistillate paleae are floret parts, so this is a doubtful target. Reject.
Same as R3016: palea is a floret part, not an inflorescence bract.
Same as R3016: paleae of florets are floret parts, not an inflorescence bract.
The leaves at the base of a pseudumbel are bracts of that inflorescence, so inflorescence bract fits only when the whole is the pseudumbel.
Pseudumbel leaf is an inflorescence bract only as part of the pseudumbel.
Plural of pseudumbel leaf, same reasoning.
A ray leaf may be a bract below a ray in a compound umbel (a bractlet). In other families a ray leaf is a leaf of a ray. Constrain it to umbels.
Leaf primordia is a listed synonym of vascular leaf primordium (plural).
A peristome filament is not a tooth. In some mosses the endostome has filaments (cilia, segments), which differ from the exostome teeth. Mapping all to tooth loses this.
Plural of peristome filament, same problem as R3024.
Filiform peristome teeth are peristome teeth. Filiform is a shape quality that should be split off.
The first leaf of a plant is a juvenile or seedling leaf only sometimes. In keys, 'first leaf' can also mean the lowest leaf of a shoot or inflorescence. The meaning depends on the context.
Première feuille has the same ambiguity as first leaf (seedling leaf or lowest leaf).
Premières feuilles has the same ambiguity as first leaf.
A glandular spot is a gland-dotted or colored patch on a surface. It is not a portion of secretory tissue. Handle as a spot with a gland quality, or reject.
Tache glanduleuse is a glandular spot or patch, same as R3030.
Tache glandulaire is a glandular spot or patch, same as R3030.
Plural of glandular spot, same as R3030.
The inner corona lobe is a distinct set of lobes in Apocynaceae and Passiflora. Mapping it to corona lobe loses inner. Only valid if no inner/outer contrast matters, so reject for now.
Inner is lost, as in R3034.
Inner is lost, as in R3034.
Coccus (coccum) is the one-seeded part of a schizocarp, such as in Euphorbiaceae. It is close to mericarp but not identical. 'coccu' looks like a truncated key, so check the match.
Involucellar bractlets form the involucel of Dipsacaceae, an epicalyx-like structure. They are not always epicalyx segments. Constrain to Dipsacaceae/Malvaceae contexts and check it by family.
Plural of involucellar bractlet, same doubt as R3038.
A floral shoot is not always the same as a reproductive shoot system. It is a rough match, but the flowering part is a branch or an axis in many floras.
Plural of floral shoot, same as R3040.
A flowering shoot is a shoot that bears flowers, which is a reproductive shoot system.
Pellucid dots are translucent dots seen in a leaf (oil glands in Rutaceae/Myrtaceae). Oil gland is a good guess for these families, but not for all taxa. Use a constraint on leaf, or reject.
Hypanthalamus does not exist as a word. It is likely a typo for hypanthium, so fix the typo upstream rather than adding a rule.
A leaf blade division can be a lobe, a segment, a leaflet or a pinna, so it is not always a lobe.
Plural of leaf blade division, same as R3045.
Divisions of the blade can be lobes, segments or leaflets, not only lobes.
A secondary pinna (second-order division) is the same as a pinnule only in a bipinnate frond or leaf. Check the order of division.
Plural of secondary pinna, same as R3048.

A throat appendage covers scales, folds or hairs in the throat of the corolla. The existing review already rejected 'corolla appendage' for the same reason, so only faucal scales in Boraginaceae would fit the corolline corona.
Throat appendages are faucal scales (Boraginaceae) or other throat outgrowths. A corona is only one reading, and the family decides which. The earlier review treated 'corolla appendage' the same way.
Cork is phellem, and PO lists 'cork' as a synonym.
A fruiting peduncle is the peduncle at the fruit stage. The stage is context, and the part is still the peduncle.
Plural of R3053: the peduncle at the fruit stage.
French for fruiting peduncle: the peduncle at the fruit stage.
'Sessile' is a quality (sessile spike versus stalked spike). Mapping the phrase to the bare spike inflorescence loses it. It should be spike inflorescence plus a sessile quality.
A stigmatic disc is a disc-shaped stigma, for example in Papaver. The part is the stigma.
French for stigmatic disc: the stigma.
'Abaxial' is a position, and it is lost when the phrase maps to the bare papilla cell. It should be papilla cell on the abaxial surface.
The target is stem cortex. Cortical cells also occur in roots and other organs, so the rule is only right for stem-like parts.
The target is stem cortex, so the rule is only right for stems. Roots also have a cortex.
The target is stem cortex, so the rule is only right for stems. 'Cortical cells' alone can belong to a root or another organ.
'Partial' (hyalodermis only partly present) is lost. Hyalodermis is also a specific hyaline cell layer, not just any epidermis.
Sclerodermis is the outer layer of thick-walled cells of the stem. It is not the whole cortex, and 'thick-walled' is lost.
Exostome teeth are the outer peristome teeth. The 'outer peristome' detail is minor, and a segment of the exostome is a tooth.
An exostome tooth is a peristome tooth of the outer row.
'Hanging' is an orientation quality (pendent), and it is lost when the phrase maps to the bare branch. It should be branch plus pendent.
'Pendent' is an orientation quality, and it is lost when the phrase maps to the bare branch. It should be branch plus pendent.
In mosses such as Fissidens, vaginant laminae are the clasping lamina parts of the leaf, not a leaf sheath. A leaf-sheath mapping would be misleading.
The ovule is the female structure, so 'female' adds nothing. The plant ovule is right.
'Collater' is a spelling variant of colleter, the glandular hair of buds and stipules (Rubiaceae).
French for colleter.
French for colleter, written without the accent.
Ostiolar bracts are the bracts that close the opening of a fig syconium. They are inflorescence bracts.
Ostiolar bracts are bracts at the ostiole of a fig syconium, and they belong to the inflorescence.
French for ostiolar bract: a bract at the opening of a fig syconium.
'Pseudo-bulb' is a spelling variant of pseudobulb.
French for pseudobulb.
'Compound' (a branched arrangement) is lost. A dichasium is a cyme, but a compound dichasium is a more specific structure.
'Lateral' is a position, and it is lost when the phrase maps to the bare bract. It should be bract plus lateral position.
'Umbellate' describes the arrangement and is lost. It is a cyme with an umbel-like form, so cyme plus umbellate arrangement.
An aciculus is a slender bristle-like prickle.
Plural of aciculus: slender prickles.
French 'acicule' is a slender prickle. 'Acicle' is an English variant.
Plural of acicle: slender prickles.
A caudex is a thick, often woody stem base or trunk, so it is a stem.
Plural of caudex: stems.
The fruit wall is the pericarp.
The fruit wall is the pericarp.
The wall of the fruit is the pericarp.
'Bearing bulbils' is a statement that bulbils are present, not a part name. It belongs to the presence pattern (bulbil present), not to a bearer rule.
Involucre-like leaves are ordinary leaves arranged like an involucre, and 'like' says they are not true involucral bracts. Mapping them to involucral bract overstates it.
Involucre-like leaves are ordinary leaves arranged like an involucre, and 'like' says they are not true involucral bracts. Mapping them to involucral bract overstates it.
Involucre-like leaves are ordinary leaves arranged like an involucre, and 'like' says they are not true involucral bracts. Mapping them to involucral bract overstates it.
'Simple' (unbranched) is a quality, and it is lost when the phrase maps to the bare trichome. It should be trichome plus simple.
'Simple' (unbranched) is a quality, and it is lost when the phrase maps to the bare trichome. It should be trichome plus simple.
A stigmatic line is a receptive line or surface on the style or stigma, not a stigma lobe. The nearest target is stigma.

Stinging hairs (Urtica and others) are stiff, needle-like trichomes that inject irritants. They are not glandular trichomes in the PO sense, and the right class is trichome, with 'stinging' as a separate quality.
A stinging hair is a trichome. Glandular trichome is the wrong type, and 'stinging' belongs as a quality.
An urticating hair is a trichome. Glandular trichome is the wrong type, and 'stinging' belongs as a quality.
Intramarginal vein is already a synonym of this PO class.
'Nerve' is the usual older word for 'vein', so this is the same part.
'Lateral' separates side pinnules from the terminal one. Mapping to plain pinnule loses that, and the earlier reviews rejected 'lateral X' parts for the same reason.
Same as R3103: the position 'latérale' is lost.
Macrospore is a synonym of megaspore, and the lexicon already lists it.
Plural of R3105.
A perianth segment is a tepal, so its margin is the tepal margin.
A perianth lobe is the free tip of a fused perianth tube. It is not a free tepal, so the lobe margin is not strictly a tepal margin.
In an umbel the primary involucre is made of involucral bracts. 'Primary' only gives the level, and the secondary involucel is a different word.
A scalelike sheath is a sheath that looks like a scale, so it may be a leaf sheath (PO_0020104) rather than a reduced scale leaf. It needs the plant group to decide.
Same as R3110.
A basal sheath is usually the leaf sheath at the base (grasses, sedges, palms). It is not a scale leaf (cataphyll).
Synandria is the plural of synandrium.
A cladoprophyll is the prophyll of a lateral branch, so it is a prophyll.
Latin form of R3114.
Plural of R3114.
Lateral petals often differ from the other petals (wings of a pea flower, orchid and Polygala flowers). Mapping to plain petal gives their traits to all petals.
Same as R3117.
Same as R3117, in French.
Same as R3117, in French.
Outer and inner tepals often differ in size, colour or hairs. Plain tepal would give outer-whorl traits to all tepals.
Same as R3121.
Same as R3121.
A venule is a vein of the smallest order. It is a leaf lamina vein only for leaves, and the order is lost. Other organs (petal, bract) also have venules.
Plural of R3124.
Oil globules are oil cavities or oil glands embedded in the tissue (Myrtaceae, Rutaceae). They are not glandular trichomes. PO oil gland is the closest class.
Plural of R3126.
Same as R3126. 'Sessile' only describes the globules.
A leaf nerve is a vein of the leaf lamina.
Plural of R3129.
Leaf-blade is a synonym of leaf lamina (leaf blade is listed in the lexicon).
Plural of R3131.
The spore capsule mouth is only for mosses. In angiosperms, 'capsule rim' is the edge of a fruit capsule (poppy, Nymphaea).
The rim of the capsule mouth is the mouth of the spore capsule.
A basal lamina is the lower part of the lamina. It is not the leaf base, which is the attachment region. The right target is the lamina with a position word.
Plural of R3135.
A struma is the swelling at the base of a moss capsule, which is the sporangium base (apophysis).
A strumose swelling is a struma.
Stilt root is already a synonym of shoot-borne root in the lexicon.
The first-order lateral veins from the midvein are the secondary veins in PO terms.
French equivalent of R3140.
'Nervure latérale' is the lateral vein of a leaf, but it also appears for sepals, bracts and corolla. It is secondary only for leaf lamina.
French 'soie' is a bristle or stiff hair on these parts. In bryology it means the seta, the stalk of the moss capsule.
Plural of R3143.
A flower stalk is normally the pedicel. A single-flowered scape would be a peduncle, but that is rarer.
Spelling variant of R3145.
Spelling variant of R3145.
Male cone is already a synonym of microsporangiate strobilus.
French equivalent of R3148.
Central vein of a leaf is the midvein.
The anther stalk is the filament.
'Stalk of anther' means the filament.
A sepal segment is normally a free sepal, or a lobe of a fused calyx. Calyx lobe is only right for the second meaning. Rejecting is safer.
Calyx segments are free sepals in some floras and fused lobes in others. Calyx lobe fits only the fused case.
Same as 'calyx segment'. The plural can mean free sepals as well as fused lobes.
A tepal lobe is a lobe of the perianth.
Plural of 'tepal lobe'.
A pit hair is a kind of hair, so trichome is right as the bearer.
Plural of 'pit hair'.
'Rootstock' is already a synonym of rhizome in PO. The same word can also mean a woody base or caudex, so the mapping is not perfect.
Spelling variant of 'root stock'.
These are the veins between the primary veins, so they are lamina veins. The more specific position is lost, but the bearer is right.
Plural of 'inter-primary vein'.
'Cyme-like' says the raceme looks like a cyme. Mapping to raceme drops that, and the term is doubtful.
Same as the singular. 'Cyme-like' is dropped.
An aculeus is a prickle.
Latin plural of aculeus.
'Bearing bulblets' is a verb phrase, not a part. The bearer is the plant or organ that carries the bulblets.
Bulblets are small bulbils. Some bulblets are underground offsets, so this is slightly loose.
A tooth on the margin of the leaf blade is a leaf lamina tooth.
The leaflet blade apex is the leaflet apex.
Alar cells sit in the basal angles of a moss leaf. 'Marginal basal cells' are the basal cells along the margin, which is a different group. No exact class exists.
Same as the singular. Marginal basal cells are not alar cells.
A perianth tooth is a small perianth lobe. In liverworts the teeth at the mouth are finer than lobes, so this is a little loose.
Plural of 'perianth tooth'.
A plantlet is a small whole plant, usually a vegetative propagule.
Plural of 'plantlet'.
An adventitious plantlet is a plantlet. The 'adventitious' part is lost, but the bearer is right.
A secondary stem is a branch. 'Secondary axis' is already a PO synonym of branch.
Plural of 'secondary stem'.
A simple cyme is a cyme. The 'simple' part is lost, but the bearer is right.
Plural of 'simple cyme'.
French for 'simple cymes'.
'With blades' is a prepositional phrase, not a part name. The bearer is the organ that has the blades.
'Acicular' is a shape (needle-like). Mapping the whole phrase to trichome drops it. The bearer should be hair and the quality acicular.
Same as the singular. The shape 'acicular' is lost.
'Adventitious root' is already a PO synonym of shoot-borne root.
'Adventitious root' is already a PO synonym of shoot-borne root.
French for adventitious roots.
An anther sac is a pollen sac. 'Anther lobe' is a synonym in PO.
Plural of 'anther sac'.
'Apice' is a variant spelling of apex, and plant organ apex covers it.
'Apices' is the plural of apex.
Basal veins are the veins that start at the base of the blade. Mapping to leaf lamina vein loses that position.
A bracteal leaf is a bract.
French for bracteal leaf.
Plural of 'bracteal leaf'.
A cauline sheath is the sheath of a stem leaf, which is a leaf sheath.
French for cauline sheaths.
Plural of 'cauline sheath'.
A compound umbellate cyme is a kind of cyme. The cyme class is correct, though it loses the umbellate and compound detail.
Epidermal cells are plant epidermal cells.
Singular form of epidermal cells. It means plant epidermal cell.
Epidermis cells are epidermal cells.
Singular form of epidermis cells. It means plant epidermal cell.
A lateral panicle is a panicle, but 'lateral' is its position. Mapping to the panicle class alone is acceptable only if the position is kept as a separate quality or context. Otherwise it is lost.
A lateral shoot is a shoot that grows from an axillary bud, which is an axillary shoot system.
A side shoot is a lateral shoot, which is an axillary shoot system.
Midrib is a listed synonym of leaf midvein. The plural is fine.
'Open' is the state of the flower (anthesis), not the part. Mapping to flower is right only if the state is kept as a quality.
'Persistent' is a quality of the style (it stays on the fruit). The bearer is the style, so the phrase should split into style and persistent.
Pinnules secondaires are secondary pinnules, which are pinnules of the second order. The pinnule class fits, though the order is lost.
A stylodium is a style, or a style branch, in Apiaceae and Poaceae. The style class is acceptable.
Plural of stylodium, which is a style.
Midnerve is the midrib, which is the leaf midvein. It needs a leaf context, but the word is normally used for leaves.
Mid-nerve is the midrib, which is the leaf midvein.
A pollen mass is a pollinium only in orchids and milkweeds. In other plants it is just a mass of pollen.
Plural of pollen mass. It is a pollinium only in orchids and milkweeds.
An antheridial branch is a moss branch that bears antheridia. It is a gametophore branch, but the function is lost. Acceptable only if the bearer is a branch of a moss.
A perigonial branch bears the male perigonia of a moss. It is a gametophore branch, but the function is lost.
A brood branch bears brood bodies (propagula). It is a gametophore branch, but the function is lost.
A brood branchlet is a small branch bearing brood bodies. The function is lost, and the size is lost too.
A propaguliferous branch is a branch that bears propagula. The function is lost.
'High papillae' is a quality (height) of papillae, not a part. The bearer would be papilla cell with a height quality, so the rule loses 'high'.
The laminal border in mosses is the leaf margin.
A superficial cortical cell layer is the outermost layer of the cortex, so it is not the whole cortex. There is no matching existing class, so it should be rejected or sent to a new term.
A superficial cortical layer is the outer layer of the cortex, so it is not the whole cortex. There is no matching existing class.
A vaginant lamina is the blade base that wraps around the stem, as in mosses. Leaf base is partly right, but 'lamina' means blade, so the mapping is doubtful.
A sheathing lamina is a blade that sheaths the stem. Leaf base is partly right, but the term is doubtful.
A vein ending can be free or can join another vein. The free ending veinlet class is correct only for free endings.
Plural of vein ending. The free ending veinlet class is correct only for free endings.
Free vein ending is a listed synonym of free ending veinlet.
A panicle of racemes is a panicle whose branches are racemes. The target is a panicle, but the raceme detail is lost.
French for panicle of racemes. It is a panicle, but the raceme detail is lost.
A pseudofascicle is a false fascicle, a cluster that looks like a fascicle. The flower fascicle class is acceptable.
French form of pseudofascicle.
Aerial root is a listed synonym of shoot-borne root.
Aerial rootlets are small aerial roots. The shoot-borne root class fits, but the small size is lost.
Cloison is a partition. It means septum in an ovary or fruit, but it can also mean a wall in a stem or a leaf.
Plural of cloison. It means septum in an ovary or fruit, but not everywhere.
Glandular spots are spots of colour or gland dots on a surface. They are not secretory tissue. A gland class with a spot quality would be better.
Glandular macules are spots on a surface, not a portion of secretory tissue.
A pellucid dot is a translucent oil gland, but only on leaves and similar parts, and not always oil. It can also be a mere translucent spot.
French for pellucid dots. They are oil glands only on some parts.
A pellucid gland is a translucent oil gland, and oil cavity is a listed synonym.
A petiolar scar is the scar left where the petiole fell, which is a leaf scar.
French for petiolar scar. It is a leaf scar.
A petiole scar is the same as a petiolar scar, which is a leaf scar.
A ramule is a small branch, and branchlet is a synonym of branch.
A ramille is a small branch in French, and branchlet is a synonym of branch.
French 'ramilles' means twigs or small branches. PO branch has 'twig' and 'branchlet' as synonyms.
Latin 'ramulus' means a small branch or twig, which PO branch covers.
'ramuli' is the plural of ramulus, a small branch or twig.

A veinule is a small vein, and PO leaf lamina vein fits when the part is a leaf. The word is also used for veinlets in sepals, petals and bracts, where the leaf lamina vein class is wrong. PO lists 'veinlet' as a synonym of secondary leaf vein, so the finest order is not certain either.
Same as R3254: a plural veinule is only a leaf lamina vein when the bearer is a leaf. Outside leaves it needs a different vein class.
'abscission layer' is already a synonym of PO abscission zone.

Culm leaves are the sheathing, often bladeless leaves on bamboo and grass culms, and they differ from ordinary cauline leaves. Mapping them to cauline leaf loses the culm-sheath meaning and the culm context, and 'culm leave' looks like a typo. Prefer the leaf class with the culm as container, or reject.
Same as R3257: 'culm leaf' is a specific sheath-like leaf of bamboo, not any cauline leaf. Use leaf with container culm instead.
Same as R3257: plural of culm leaf, which is more specific than cauline leaf.

A sinker is a specialised root, such as a descending parasitic or haustorial root, or a water-seeking root. PO root is too general. A bare 'sinker' can also mean a fishing weight or a fruit-tree shoot, so the word is ambiguous. Reject, or use a sinker-root class if one is created.
A sinker root is a specific root type, usually a vertical root descending from a horizontal root. Mapping it to plain root loses that meaning. A constraint on the container would not fix it.
Same as R3261: plural of sinker root, which is a specific kind of root.
Same as R3260: 'sinkers' is ambiguous. In a plant context it means descending special roots, which plain PO root does not capture.
Ovary wall is the plain label of PO plant ovary wall.
'paroi de l'ovaire' is the French for ovary wall.

Bole is already a PO stem synonym and means the trunk of a tree. It is correct for trees and shrubs. It is wrong in the sense of a bole of a leaf bundle or a fungus-related use, and should not match other parts.

A resin dot is a resin-filled gland or secretory cavity visible on the surface, and mapping it to 'portion of secretory tissue' loses the resin and the dot shape. PO lists 'gland' as a synonym of this class, so a resin-dot mapping is a stretch. Prefer a gland class, or reject.
Same as R3267: a resin dot is a resin gland, not secretory tissue in general.
Same as R3267: the spaced form of resin-dot.

A panicled cyme is a cyme arranged in a panicle, so it has both a cyme and a panicle part. PO cyme inflorescence loses the panicle arrangement, which is a quality of the inflorescence. Better to map to cyme inflorescence with an arrangement quality, or leave it as a rule that adds the quality.
Same as R3270: 'paniculate cyme' loses the panicle arrangement.

A sporangiophore is a stalk that bears sporangia (in Equisetum, fungi). It is not a sporophyll, which is a leaf that bears sporangia. In Equisetum the sporangiophores are peltate scales, so they are not leaf-like in the PO sense. Reject, or ask for a new class.
Same as R3272: plural of sporangiophore, which is not a sporophyll.
'cormlet' is already a synonym for corm in PO (cormel). It is a small corm.
'cormel' is already a PO corm synonym.

A craspedium is the loment-like fruit of Mimosoideae (e.g. Entada) whose segments break away and leave the persistent frame (replum). It is a kind of loment. The match to loment fruit is close, though not perfect.
Plural of craspedium, with the same reasoning as R3276.

'secondary venation' means the pattern of secondary veins, which is a quality-like property of the leaf, not one organ. Mapping it to the secondary leaf vein class is a partial match. The venation pattern should be treated as a leaf quality, not a bearer.

Costal veins are veins along the leaf margin or the main rib, as in grasses and palms. They are not the same as secondary veins. In some floras 'costal' secondary veins arise from the midrib, but this is not reliable.
Same as R3279: plural of costal vein, which is not the same as secondary vein.

PO second order inflorescence axis has 'first order inflorescence branch' as a synonym, so it works for inflorescences. In other contexts a first-order branch is just a branch on a tree or shoot, where PO branch is right.
Same as R3281: plural form, and only correct when the part belongs to an inflorescence.

A fruiting head is a head-like fruit cluster, for example in Asteraceae. PO infructescence is the right class, but it loses the head form, which is a shape quality. Marginal: acceptable as a bearer if the shape is not required.
Same as R3283: 'fruit head' is an infructescence of head form.
Same as R3283: plural of fruiting head.

An anterior lip is the lower lip in a two-lipped corolla, so it fits the corolla lip when the whole is a corolla. A bare 'anterior lip' could also be a calyx lip or an orchid labellum. The class should be used only for corollas.
A lower lip is the anterior lip of a corolla, but 'lower lip' is also used for the calyx in Lamiaceae and for the orchid labellum. It is correct only when the whole is the corolla.

'with palea' is a phrase meaning 'has a palea', not a name for the part. It looks like a presence statement and should become an entity-presence rule on palea. Also, PO_0009038 is labelled palea but the lexicon lists palea as a synonym of inflorescence bract PO_0009054, so check the ID.

Floral scales in Cyperaceae and in conifers are bract-like structures, but in other plants 'floral scale' can be a perianth scale, such as the lodicule or a tepal-like scale in Juncaceae. Mapping every use to inflorescence bract loses that. Use only when the part is a spikelet or cone.
Same as R3289: plural of floral scale.
Oil tubes are the vittae of Apiaceae fruits, so the vitta class fits.
Spaced form of oil-tube, which is a vitta.
Plural of oil-tube, which is a vitta.
A staminal disc is a nectary disc around or inside the stamens. A synandrium is a fusion of stamens, so it is a different thing. Reject, or use a nectary disc class.
Same as R3294: an androecial disc is a disc-like structure of the androecium, not a synandrium.

A calycophyll is a petaloid, enlarged calyx lobe, as in Mussaenda. It is a particular type of calyx lobe, so mapping it to a plain calyx lobe loses the enlarged, leaf-like form. Possibly acceptable only with a quality added.
'enlarged calyx lobe' includes a size quality (enlarged). Mapping it to calyx lobe alone drops the enlarged meaning. It should be calyx lobe plus a size quality.

PO vascular bundle has 'vein' as a synonym, so strand fits when the part is a vascular bundle. 'Vascular strand' can also mean a single xylem or phloem strand, or a fibre strand, so it is not always a whole bundle.
Same as R3298: plural of vascular strand.

A chalk gland is a gland that secretes calcium carbonate (lime scales), as in Saxifraga. It is a type of hydathode in some cases, but not all hydathodes secrete chalk. Mapping it to hydathode loses the chalk-secretion meaning, though the match is plausible.
The lime or chalk glands of Limonium and similar plants are water-and-salt glands, which is what a hydathode is.
Same as 'lime gland'. Chalk glands secrete lime-rich water, so they are hydathodes.
Perigon (perigone) is another word for perianth.
A subleaflet is the ultimate segment of a twice-compound leaf, which is a pinnule.
Plural of 'subleaflet'. Same reasoning.
Oil tubes in Apiaceae fruits are vittae.
Plural of 'oiltube'. Same reasoning.
The aerial part of a plant is its shoot system, including stems, leaves and flowers.
French plural of 'aerial part'. Same reasoning.
Plural of 'aerial part'. Same reasoning.
'Laminar' says the colleter sits on the leaf blade. The target loses that. Use colleter with leaf lamina as the container.
Plural of 'laminar colleter'. The position on the leaf blade is lost.
Wool is a dense covering of long, tangled hairs, so trichome is acceptable as the bearer. A portion of indumentum would be more exact.
'Woolly' is a quality (lanate or tomentose). The bearer rule would drop it. The bearer is trichome and the quality needs to be kept.
'Spathe' is already a synonym of inflorescence bract in PO, and a spathe bract is the same kind of part.
A fruit cup, as in Fagaceae, is a cupule.
An acorn cup is a cupule.

In Asteraceae the calyculus is a set of outer, short phyllaries, which are involucral bracts. In Malvaceae and Dipsacaceae the calyculus or epicalyx bracts are bracteoles below the calyx, which are plain bracts.
French form of 'calicle bract'. Same family-dependent problem.
Same as 'calicle bract'. Only correct for Asteraceae-type heads. Elsewhere it is an epicalyx bract (PO_0009055).
A grappling-hook is a hooked hair, so a trichome. The 'simple' type is a separate quality.
Hooked trichome with a simple form. Trichome is correct.
A raylet is a branch of a partial umbel, a higher-order inflorescence axis.
Plural of 'raylet'. Same reasoning.
A grappling-hook is a hooked hair, so a trichome. 'Complex' is a separate quality.
Hooked trichome with a complex form. Trichome is correct.
A pseudolocule is a false locule, a cavity without the true locule structure. Mapping it to locule loses the 'false' part.
A false locule is not a true locule, and the 'false' part is lost.
'Pseudoloculed' is an adjective, meaning having false locules. It is a quality word, not a part name, so it should not be a bearer.
'Rostella' is the Latin plural of rostellum.
'Rostelle' is the French word for rostellum.
A perianth blade is the limb of a fused perianth, not a tepal. No existing class fits it. Leave it unmapped, or use perianth with a limb container.
This is the blade of a perianth segment, not the whole tepal. The 'blade' part is lost. A tepal lamina class would be better.
A 'central flower' is the middle flower of a cluster, as in cymes and umbels. It is not necessarily a disk flower. Use flower.
Ramenta are thin scales on fern axes, which are trichome-like outgrowths. The match is loose but acceptable.
Singular of 'ramenta'. Same reasoning.
A coronal appendage is a structure on the corona (horn, scale, tooth), not the corona lobe itself.
A coronal appendage is a structure on the corona, not the corona lobe itself.
A tack-gland is a gland, and 'gland' is a synonym of PO_0005656.
Plural of 'tack-gland'. Same reasoning.
'Tack-shaped' is a shape quality of the gland, and the rule would drop it. The bearer is the gland, and the shape stays as the quality.
A spray is a branched inflorescence, but it can also be a leafy shoot or twig, so inflorescence is not always right.
Plural of 'spray'. Same problem: it is not always an inflorescence.
A labellum segment is a lobe of the labellum.
Plural of 'labellum segment'. Same reasoning.
French for labellum segment.
A bracteal leaf is a bract. The singular 'leave' looks like a typo for 'leaf' or 'leaves'.
A floral bud scale is a bud scale leaf, here of a flower bud.
Plural of 'floral bud scale'. Same reasoning.
A flower bud scale is a bud scale leaf, here of a flower bud.
Anther cap is the anther cap class.
Crozier is already a synonym of vascular leaf in PO. It is a young coiled frond.
Plural of crozier. Same as R3352.
A spadicle is a small spadix or a spadix branch. Spadix inflorescence is the nearest class.
Plural of spadicle. Same as R3354.
A rachis article is a segment of the inflorescence rachis, mostly in grasses. That is an inflorescence axis internode.
French form of rachis article. Same as R3356.
The word 'disk' carries the shape of the stigma, for example the Papaver stigmatic disc. Mapping to stigma loses it. Not mapped to stigma alone.
A filament tube is the tube formed by fused filaments, which is the staminal tube.
Hyphenated spelling of filament tube.
A filament column is the fused filaments, which is the staminal tube.
A subraceme is a small raceme.
A partial raceme is a raceme unit inside a compound inflorescence.
The beak is the persistent style, mostly in fruits.
Same as R3364.
French form of style beak. Same as R3364.
A partial peduncle is the stalk of a partial inflorescence. That is a higher-order inflorescence axis.
Plural of partial peduncle.
French form of partial peduncle.
A floret is a small flower, and functionally staminate means it works as a male flower.
Functionally male means staminate in function.
Same as R3370.
Tubular florets are the disc florets of Asteraceae. The word 'floret' fixes the family.
Plural of tubular floret.
